_note: the curated dossiers (engine/biology/dossiers/), drafts until approved

Absol.summary: Absol is a white, horned mountain quadruped (1.2 m, 47 kg) that senses subtle changes in the sky and the land and foretells natural disasters. It rarely comes down from its harsh, rugged mountains, and when it does appear before people it has come to warn them. Because disasters followed its appearances it was long mistaken for a bringer of doom, and a rumour that its horn senses disaster made it a target, so it fled deeper into the mountains. It lives a hundred years or more. In Johto it is not native: HeartGold and SoulSilver have it only through the Hoenn radio broadcast, which puts it in nearly every cave, including the Ice Path and the Dark Cave at Blackthorn.

anatomy.text: A quadruped of 1.2 m and 47 kg, white, Dark type, with a horn.
It is long-lived, with a life span of 100 years or more.
Whether the horn is a sense organ is only a rumour (359.6); no entry states it as fact.

diet.text: No entry says what Absol eats.
Its wild moves are mostly cutting and biting attacks (Slash, Night Slash, Psycho Cut, Bite, Pursuit), which suggests a predator, but that is a reading of moves.
diet.note: The machine reading's 'predator' came from its Dark type alone.

habitat.text: It lives in a harsh, rugged mountain environment and very rarely ventures down.
In Hoenn it is on Route 120 (8%, all three Hoenn games); in Diamond and Pearl only during a swarm on Route 213; in Platinum on the snowy exterior of Mt. Coronet, in snowfall and blizzard.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it appears only when the Hoenn radio broadcast is playing, at 20% in almost every cave in Johto and Kanto: Union Cave, Slowpoke Well, Mt. Mortar, the Ice Path, Dark Cave, Mt. Silver, Victory Road and more. That is one radio slot applied to every cave, not evidence of a cave-dwelling population.
Platinum's snowy Mt. Coronet tables suit its mountain entries best: high, cold and rugged.

behavior.text: It foretells natural disasters by sharply sensing subtle changes in the sky and the land.
It appears before people when it senses a coming disaster, and does so only to warn them.
Its activity pattern is unknown; none of its encounter tables split by time of day.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or territory.
Its base friendship is 35, half the usual 70, and its catch rate is low (30): in game terms a wary, hard-to-win animal, which fits its history with people.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 25 egg cycles, an even sex ratio.
A century-long life with a longer incubation than most species here suggests a slow-breeding animal, but nothing describes how often it breeds.

defense.text: Its first defence is distance: it lives high in rugged mountains and, once hunted, fled deeper into them.
Its wild repertoire favours avoiding blows: Double Team (Lv 33), Detect (Lv 49) and Sucker Punch (Lv 44), which strikes first only when the foe is about to attack.
Pressure makes opponents spend their moves faster, and Super Luck raises its chance of a critical hit.

senses.text: It senses even subtle changes in the sky and the land, which is how it predicts disasters; which changes it feels is not said.
senses.analogy: Common toads were recorded abandoning a breeding site in the days before the 2009 L'Aquila earthquake in Italy, but whether any animal can reliably sense coming earthquakes remains unproven.

senses.text: The horn as its sensor is a rumour, and the rumour is what made it a target.

life_cycle.text: Absol doesn't evolve and has no pre-evolution; its growth rate is medium slow.
It lives 100 years or more.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Foresight in move form: Future Sight (Lv 41), an attack that lands two turns later, matches its foretelling.
Blades: Razor Wind (Lv 17), Slash (Lv 36), Night Slash (Lv 52) and Psycho Cut (Lv 60).
Perish Song (Lv 65), which makes everything that hears it faint after three turns, is a grim fit for an animal known as the Disaster Pokémon; no entry links the two.

ecology.text: A rare, long-lived mountain animal; its place in the food web is unknown because its diet is never stated.
On Hoenn's Route 120 it shares the grass with Poochyena and Mightyena, the other Dark-type quadrupeds there; on Platinum's Mt. Coronet slopes with Snover and Abomasnow.

humans.text: Disasters followed its appearances before people, so it became known as the Disaster Pokémon.
That reputation was a mistake: it appears because it senses disaster coming, and comes to warn people.
A rumour that its horn senses disaster made it a target, and it fled deep into the mountains.
humans.analogy: Rhinoceroses have been hunted close to extinction for their horn, prized on the strength of unfounded beliefs about its powers.

humans.text: Its retreat into the mountains may therefore be partly the result of persecution rather than a natural preference.

homestead.text: Disaster warning for a mountain homestead: avalanche, rockfall, flood or earthquake. It senses changes in sky and land, and comes to people to warn them.
Make sure neighbours in Blackthorn know what an Absol's appearance means, so that the warning isn't mistaken for a curse.
Its horn must never be treated as a medicine or charm; that rumour is what drove it into the mountains.
Needs: high, rugged ground nearby and room to keep its distance; it is wary by nature and slow to trust.
Flash, a taught move, would make it a light source.
A 100-year lifespan means an Absol taken in may outlive its keeper; the homestead would need to plan for its care across generations.

niche.foraging: not described
niche.note: Diet is never stated. Its HeartGold and SoulSilver cave records come from the Hoenn radio, not a native population.

relationships.note: Route 120 in Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald.
Mt. Coronet's snowy exterior in Platinum.
Mt. Coronet's snowy exterior in Platinum.

ecotypes.name: Horn-charger
ecotypes.reading: Megahorn is a ramming horn strike, Zen Headbutt a head blow, and Double-Edge a full-weight charge. A lineage that uses its horn as a weapon rather than a sensor, meeting threats head-on. Fits contested ridges where retreat is not possible.
ecotypes.behavior: Lowers its horn and charges instead of slipping away.

ecotypes.name: Decoy shadow
ecotypes.reading: Substitute leaves a decoy, Baton Pass hands off and withdraws, and Feint Attack strikes unseen. A lineage built to avoid being taken: decoys and disappearances in place of fighting. Fits mountains where it is hunted, as the Platinum entry describes.
ecotypes.behavior: Seen once, then gone; trackers follow the wrong trail.

ecotypes.name: Snowfield watcher
ecotypes.reading: Curse trades speed for toughness, and Mean Look pins a target with a stare so it can't flee. A lineage that holds still on open snow and stares down whatever approaches, rather than retreating. Fits high snowfields like Platinum's Mt. Coronet slopes.
ecotypes.behavior: Stands motionless on a snow ridge, watching the valley for days.

open_questions: What does Absol eat?
What exactly does it sense: pressure, ground vibration, animal behaviour, something else? And is the horn involved?
Did it always live high in the mountains (359.2), or was it driven there by persecution (359.6)?
How often does it breed, given its century-long life?
Would a wild Absol near Blackthorn warn the homestead, or only people it already knows?
Is it truly absent from Johto's wild, apart from the radio broadcast?

contradictions.note: Ruby (359.1) reports that disasters follow its appearances and names it accordingly; FireRed, LeafGreen, Diamond and Pearl (359.4, 359.5) say this was a mistake and that it comes to warn. The later entries correct the earlier one.
Sapphire (359.2) presents the harsh mountains as its home; Platinum (359.6) says it fled deep into the mountains after being hunted, implying it once lived lower down.

folklore.text: It is rumoured to sense disasters with its horn.
folklore.note: The rumour, not the horn, is what made it a target.

folklore.text: It was believed to bring disasters, and so was called a doom-bringer.
folklore.note: 359.4 calls the belief a mistake.

Alakazam.summary: Alakazam is a humanoid Psychic Pokémon whose brain never stops growing: its brain cells multiply until it dies, it forgets nothing, and its head becomes too heavy for its neck, so it holds it up by psychokinesis. Its muscles are very weak, it moves its body with psychic power, and it would rather not fight hand to hand. It is the end of a line that begins with Abra, which sleeps 18 hours a day and teleports away from danger even in its sleep. Alakazam only forms when a Kadabra is traded between people, so no Gen I–IV game has a wild one.

anatomy.text: A humanoid body of 1.5 m and 48 kg, Psychic type; it holds spoons in its hands.
Its brain cells multiply continually until it dies, and the brain keeps growing.
The head becomes far too heavy for its neck, so it holds its head up with psychokinetic power.
Its muscles are very weak; it moves its body by psychic power.
Alakazam (48 kg) weighs less than Kadabra (56.5 kg) although it is taller, consistent with an animal that loses muscle as it comes to rely on psychokinesis.
Its brain is described as able to outperform a supercomputer.

diet.text: No entry for any stage says what the line eats.
A brain that never stops growing must be expensive to run, so its energy needs are probably high; how it meets them is unrecorded.
diet.note: The machine reading's 'psychotroph' came from its Psychic type alone.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: urban.
Alakazam is never wild in Gen I–IV, because it forms only when a Kadabra is traded.

Abra is widespread: grassy routes in Kanto and Johto (in HeartGold and SoulSilver, Routes 34, 35, 5, 6, 8, 24 and 25), Granite Cave and Route 116 in Hoenn, Routes 203 and 215 in Sinnoh. Kadabra is wild on Kanto's Route 8, in Cerulean Cave, and in Sinnoh's Victory Road and Route 215.
Abra is also a Game Corner prize in Celadon City and Goldenrod City, and in Diamond, Pearl and Platinum a person in Oreburgh City trades one for a Machop.

behavior.text: It calculates many things in order to gain the edge in every battle.
It does not like physical attacks, and uses extrasensory powers to defeat foes instead.
Abra sleeps 18 hours a day, because using psychic power strains its brain; without that sleep it loses its telekinetic powers.
Whether the adult also needs that much sleep is not stated, but a brain that keeps growing gives no reason to expect less.
Activity pattern: Abra is on Gold, Silver and Crystal's tables morning, day and night alike, so the line's waking hours are not tied to the time of day.

social.text: No entry describes how Alakazam live with their own kind.

reproduction.text: Human-Like egg group, 20 egg cycles, 75% male.
Its superb memory lets it recall everything it has experienced from birth.
Nothing describes breeding or care of young.

defense.text: It avoids physical fighting and defeats foes with extrasensory power.
The line's first defence is to leave: Abra senses or reads impending danger and teleports to safety, even while asleep, putting itself into a trance so that it can.
When Abra teleports at random it creates the illusion of copies of itself.
Teleport is still in Alakazam's level-up set (Lv 1), alongside Reflect (Lv 28) and Recover (Lv 30).
Inner Focus keeps it from flinching, and Synchronize passes poison, burns or paralysis back to an attacker.

senses.text: Closing both its eyes heightens all its other senses, letting it use its abilities to their extremes.
Abra keeps a telepathic radar even while asleep and can sense foes in its sleep.
Kadabra gives off twice as many alpha particles when it closes its eyes, the same eyes-closed heightening seen in the adult.

life_cycle.text: Abra (0.9 m, 19.5 kg) becomes Kadabra at level 16 (1.3 m, 56.5 kg), and Kadabra becomes Alakazam (1.5 m, 48 kg) only when traded.
Read biologically, the final stage depends on exchange between people. No Alakazam can arise in a wild population, which fits its absence from every encounter table.
Kadabra emits alpha waves that cause headaches in people close by, make machines malfunction and ruin precision devices; it holds a silver spoon to amplify those waves.
Kadabra's psychic power grows stronger the more danger it faces, and many odd things happen near it, such as clocks running backwards and eerie shadows on television screens.
Development runs from a sleeping, fleeing juvenile, through a disruptive, spoon-focused adolescent, to an adult whose growing brain outstrips its body.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Abra's only level-up move is Teleport: the juvenile's entire repertoire is escape.
Kinesis (Lv 1), in which the user bends a spoon to distract the target, is the spoon of the Kadabra entries in move form.

Its level-up attacks are all psychic: Confusion, Psybeam (Lv 24), Psycho Cut (Lv 34), Psychic (Lv 40) and Future Sight (Lv 42); Calm Mind (Lv 36) and Miracle Eye (Lv 22) fit a mind that calculates and sees through tricks.
This is a repertoire nothing observes in the wild, since no wild Alakazam exists in these games.

ecology.text: Its role in a wild community is unknown, and in the games' terms it has none: it exists only through trade.
Abra, which is wild and common, is a small prey-sized animal that survives by sleeping, sensing and teleporting rather than hiding or fighting.

humans.text: Only people with a particularly strong psyche can hope to train a Kadabra.
Its whole final stage is created by people trading it, which makes Alakazam as much a product of human exchange as of biology.

homestead.text: An emergency exit: Teleport is part of its own repertoire and gets everyone out fast.
Early warning: the line senses danger before it arrives, and the adult's senses sharpen further when it closes its eyes.
Fine handling: it holds spoons and moves its body by psychokinesis, so delicate work at a distance is plausible.
The homestead's memory: an animal that forgets nothing could keep the breeding records in its head.
Not a labourer: its muscles are very weak.
Keep a Kadabra away from incubators, radios and any precision equipment: its alpha waves make machines malfunction. Whether Alakazam does the same is not stated.

microhabitat: grassy routes and caves (Abra and Kadabra)
niche.foraging: not described
niche.note: Diet is never stated. Alakazam has no wild niche in these games.

relationships.note: Kadabra uses one to amplify its alpha waves; Alakazam's spoons are said to be made by its psychic powers.

ecotypes.name: Elemental fist
ecotypes.reading: Three punches that each carry an element. A lineage that does fight hand to hand, making up for weak muscles with fire, cold and charge delivered on contact. It runs against the adult's dislike of physical attacks (65.9). Fits close quarters, such as caves like Granite Cave where foes come within reach before they can be sensed.
ecotypes.behavior: Lets a foe close in, then strikes once, hard, with whatever element suits.

ecotypes.name: Walled sleeper
ecotypes.reading: Barrier raises a sharp defensive wall and Guard Swap trades defensive advantages with a foe. A lineage that protects its long sleep with walls instead of teleporting away. Fits narrow caves and crowded towns where teleporting at random is risky.
ecotypes.behavior: Sleeps behind a barrier and doesn't flee.

ecotypes.name: Trickster
ecotypes.reading: Encore locks a foe into repeating its last move, Knock Off strips what it holds, and Power Trick swaps the user's own attack and defence. A calculating lineage that disarms and controls foes instead of overpowering them, the 'calculates many things' of 65.5 put to work. Fits towns, where people and their objects are always within reach.
ecotypes.behavior: Makes its opponent predictable, then takes its things.

open_questions: What does the line eat, and how does it fuel a brain that never stops growing?
Does the adult still sleep 18 hours a day, as Abra does?
Where do its spoons come from: found, made, or psychically created (65.13)?
Does Alakazam make machines malfunction, as Kadabra does?
Could Alakazam ever arise without people trading it?
What is its memory of: its own life (65.11), or 'everything that has occurred in the world' (65.7)?
Was there ever a boy who became a Kadabra? (see folklore and contradictions)

contradictions.note: Red, Blue and LeafGreen (65.1, 65.10) give an IQ of 5,000 as something 'it is said'; Crystal and Sapphire (65.5, 65.7) state it as fact; Diamond (65.11) says it exceeds 5,000.
Diamond (65.11) says it recalls everything it has experienced since birth; Sapphire (65.7) says it has a thorough memory of everything that has occurred in the world, which is a much larger claim.

contradictions.topic: The boy who became a Kadabra
contradictions.note: Emerald (64.8) reports it as a rumour; FireRed (64.9) narrates it as an event.

folklore.text: Its IQ is said to be about 5,000.
folklore.note: Other entries state the figure as fact (see contradictions).

folklore.text: The spoons in its hands are said to have been created by its psychic powers.
A boy with psychic abilities is rumoured to have turned into a Kadabra while helping with research into extrasensory powers; another version has him wake one morning transformed.
folklore.note: Line folklore, from Kadabra's entries.

folklore.text: Without its spoon, Kadabra is said to have only half its usual telekinetic power, and seeing the shadow it casts on television screens is said to bring bad luck.
folklore.note: Line folklore.

Altaria.summary: Altaria is a light, cloud-winged dragon (1.1 m, 20.6 kg) that rides updrafts high into the sky and looks like a fluffy cloud in flight. It sings or hums in a clear soprano that leaves listeners feeling as if they are dreaming, and a beautiful melody heard deep in the mountains, far from people, is Altaria humming. It can also launch intensely hot fireballs, and an Altaria that bonds with a person wraps them in its soft wings and hums. It grows from Swablu, a tame, fastidiously clean little bird that sits on people's heads and whose flocks move closer to towns each spring after a hungry winter. In HeartGold and SoulSilver, Swablu appears only as a swarm on Route 45, the road below Blackthorn.

anatomy.text: A light, winged body of 1.1 m and 20.6 kg, Dragon and Flying type.
Its wings are like cotton clouds: soft and buoyant enough to catch updrafts and soar.
It launches intensely hot fireballs from its mouth.
A clear soprano voice.
Swablu's wings are light, fluffy tufts like cotton clouds.

diet.text: No entry says what either stage eats.
Food is seasonal for the line: little is available to Swablu in winter, and its flocks move closer to towns in spring.
Its level-up moves include Peck and Pluck (both at Lv 1), and Pluck eats a target's Berry; Natural Gift (Lv 32) also needs a held Berry. Together they hint that fruit is part of its diet.
diet.note: Moves, not entries. The machine reading's 'predator' came from its Dragon type alone.

habitat.text: The sky: it flies, dances and wheels among white, billowing clouds.
It lives deep in mountains far from people.
The Gen 3 Pokédex files the line under forest, which no Altaria entry mentions; Swablu's town visits and stream baths fit forest edges better.
Wild Altaria occur only on the fifth floor of Sky Pillar in Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald, at 6%.

Swablu lives on Hoenn's Routes 114 and 115, by Poké Radar on Sinnoh's Route 211 (Diamond, Pearl) or on Route 210 (Platinum), and in HeartGold and SoulSilver only as a swarm on Route 45, the mountain road south of Blackthorn.
habitat.note: Route 45's position is from the game map.

behavior.text: It sings and hums, and its melodies make listeners feel as if they are in a dream.
Its flight is a display: it dances and wheels through the sky among clouds.
Swablu is fastidious: it constantly grooms its wings, wipes and polishes dirty things with them, can't relax if it or its surroundings are dirty, and showers in a stream or springwater when soiled.
Its activity pattern is unknown.

social.text: Swablu lives in flocks that move closer to towns in spring.
Swablu is not frightened of people and loves to sit on their heads like a cotton hat.
An Altaria that bonds with a person gently wraps them in its soft wings, then hums.
The humming heard far from people suggests adults spend at least some time alone in the mountains.

reproduction.text: Flying and Dragon egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio.
Nothing describes courtship, nests or care of young. Its dancing flight and song are the obvious candidates for courtship displays, but no entry says so.
reproduction.note: Song and display flight serve courtship in many birds; that is a general expectation, not canon.

defense.text: Fire: it launches intensely hot fireballs.
Song as defence: Sing (Lv 9) puts the target to sleep, which is the 'dreamy wonderment' of its entries in move form; Perish Song (Lv 62) makes everything that hears it faint after three turns.

Safeguard (Lv 18), Mist (Lv 23) and Refresh (Lv 46) protect it from status harm and stat loss; Natural Cure clears its status problems when it withdraws. With Swablu's grooming, the line looks built to stay clean of ailments.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: Swablu (0.4 m, 1.2 kg, Normal and Flying) becomes Altaria at level 35 (1.1 m, 20.6 kg, Dragon and Flying), about seventeen times heavier.
Development moves it from a tame, flocking bird of forest edges and towns to a mostly solitary singer of the high mountains and sky, though adults still bond with people.
Its growth rate is erratic: slow at first, then very fast.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Dragon Dance (Lv 39) is the move form of its dancing, wheeling flight, and Dragon Breath, learned at Lv 35 as it evolves, its fiery breath.
Bill: Peck, Pluck and Fury Attack (Lv 13).
Flight attacks: Sky Attack (Lv 70) by level-up; Fly is a machine move taught by people.

ecology.text: Swablu flocks move seasonally, towards towns in spring after a hungry winter, so they bring a pulse of birds into settled land each year.
If the line eats fruit, as Pluck and Natural Gift hint, Swablu flocks could disperse seeds between forest and towns.
ecology.note: Diet is never stated.

ecology.text: Its trophic position is unknown.

humans.text: Swablu is tame with people and perches on their heads; Altaria bonds with people and envelops them in its wings.
Its humming is something people recognise and seek out in the mountains.

homestead.text: A calming presence: its humming makes people feel as if they're dreaming, and a bonded Altaria wraps its person in its wings.
Air errands: Fly is a taught move, but at 20.6 kg it is light for carrying an adult rider, so scouting and carrying small items suit it better.
A heat source in a pinch: it launches intensely hot fireballs. Whether it can give steady, gentle heat is not known.
homestead.note: The capability records list heat from this entry; nothing says it can be controlled.

homestead.text: Swablu would clean: it wipes and polishes dirty things with its wings of its own accord. Whether it would do so where it is asked is untested.
homestead.note: A canon habit; turning it into a job is an assumption.

homestead.text: Needs: clean running or spring water to bathe in, and extra food in late winter, when Swablu go hungry.
A spring arrival: in Johto, wild Swablu turn up only as a Route 45 swarm, so a flock near Blackthorn is an event, not a fixture.

niche.foraging: not described
niche.note: Diet is never stated; Pluck and Natural Gift hint at fruit.

relationships.note: Swablu bathes in them.
Swablu flocks move closer to towns in spring after a winter of scarce food; what they take there is not said.
Route 45 in HeartGold, where Swablu appears as a swarm.
Route 45 in HeartGold and SoulSilver.

ecotypes.name: Cloud dancer
ecotypes.reading: Feather Dance buries an attacker in down, blunting its attack, and Agility is a burst of speed. A lineage that turns its dancing flight (334.1) into defence, shedding down and outflying trouble. Fits open mountain skies with strong updrafts.
ecotypes.behavior: Answers a threat with a dazzling, feather-shedding display and then is gone.

ecotypes.name: Mobbing flock
ecotypes.reading: Pursuit strikes a fleeing target, Rage builds with every hit taken, and Dragon Rush is a full-body charge. A lineage whose flocks chase and harry intruders together rather than hiding. Fits forest edges near towns, where Swablu flocks gather in spring and predators follow them.
ecotypes.behavior: The whole flock turns on a hawk and drives it off.
ecotypes.analogy: Many small songbirds mob predators in groups, harassing them until they leave.

ecotypes.name: Fog-bank flock
ecotypes.reading: Haze clears every stat change on the field, and Power Swap trades the user's attacking changes with a foe's. A lineage that neutralises an attacker's advantage rather than fighting it, at home in cloud and mist. Fits cloud-wrapped peaks where visibility is poor and fights are short and confused.
ecotypes.behavior: Disappears into cloud; whatever followed it comes out no stronger than it went in.

open_questions: What does the line eat? Pluck and Natural Gift hint at fruit.
Is it a forest animal (Gen 3 habitat) or a mountain and sky animal (334.4)?
Where do Swablu flocks spend winter, and why is food scarce for them then?
Do its song and dance serve courtship?
Can a 20.6 kg animal really carry a person?
Is its fire usable as gentle heat, or only as attack?
Does Perish Song, a level-up move, reflect anything real about its singing?

contradictions.topic: Near people or far from them
contradictions.note: FireRed and LeafGreen (334.4) place Altaria deep in mountains far from people; Ruby and Emerald (333.1, 333.3) have Swablu unafraid of people and moving towards towns, and Platinum (334.6) has Altaria bonding with a person. Different stages and situations, but the line's relationship with people is never squared.

Ampharos.summary: Ampharos is the light-bearer of the Wool line: the tip of its tail shines brightly enough to be seen far away, over open sea at night, and people have treasured it as a beacon since ancient times, using it to send signals and to guide the lost. Its electricity begins in the young: Mareep's fleece builds static as the wool rubs together, and the more charge it holds, the brighter its tail glows. Flaaffy grows a rubbery, insulated hide and loses patches of wool to the charge it stores. Ampharos itself is never found wild in Gen I–IV, so everything about its wild life is read through Mareep and Flaaffy on Johto's grassy routes.

anatomy.text: An upright, tailed body of 1.4 m and 61.5 kg, Electric type, with a light at the tip of its tail.
The tail's tip shines brightly enough to be seen from far away.
In Mareep the wool is a generator: the fluffy coat rubs together and builds a static charge, and the fleece doubles in volume as charge builds.
anatomy.analogy: Rubbing wool really does build static charge (the triboelectric effect), and charged fibres repel one another and stand apart, which is why charged fleece would fluff up.

anatomy.text: Flaaffy's skin is rubbery and resists electricity, and its bare, slick patches are shielded against it; that insulation is what lets it store a lot of charge in its fur.

No Ampharos entry mentions wool. Flaaffy already has bare patches from storing too much electricity, and its wool changes so that a little produces more static; the line's trend is towards less fleece and more stored charge.

diet.text: No entry for any stage says what it eats.
A woolly grassland quadruped as a juvenile, it plausibly grazes; its electricity is described as made by friction in its wool, not taken in from outside, so it isn't fed by electricity.
diet.note: The machine reading's 'electrotroph' came from its Electric type alone; the entries describe self-generated static.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for every stage: grassland.
Its light can be seen far across the ocean's surface after dark, which puts at least some Ampharos on coasts.
Ampharos isn't found in the wild in any Gen I–IV game. Mareep lives on Johto's Routes 32, 42 and 43 in Gold, Silver, HeartGold and SoulSilver, and Flaaffy on Routes 42 and 43.
The encounter data has no Crystal records for any stage of the line, which is either a real gap in Crystal or a gap in the data.

Elsewhere it is marginal: Mareep only in Emerald's Safari Zone, in a variant table (B) of Altering Cave in FireRed and LeafGreen, and by Poké Radar at Sinnoh's Valley Windworks; Flaaffy by Poké Radar on Route 222. HeartGold and SoulSilver also give a Mareep egg in Violet City for a password, and have it in the Johto Safari Zone's forest blocks.

behavior.text: Mareep is on the Route 32 and 43 tables morning, day and night, at a lower rate at night; Ampharos's light is noticed 'when it gets dark'. It seems to be about by day and night alike.
Its glow tracks its charge: the more static it has built, the brighter the tail.
No entry describes the adult's day-to-day behaviour.

social.text: No entry describes flocks, pairs or hierarchy for any stage.
A light visible from far off, carried by a grassland animal, could serve to keep a scattered group in contact at night; nothing in canon says Ampharos signal to each other.
social.note: People used its light for signalling (181.4); whether Ampharos do is unknown.

reproduction.text: Monster and Field egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio.
Nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding or care of young.

defense.text: Static: touching any stage risks a shock, and in the games contact may paralyse.
Flaaffy fires hair that zaps on impact, a projectile defence built from its wool.
Cotton Spore, a level-up move of every stage (Lv 19–20), fits that wool-shedding defence: it slows an attacker with cotton-like fibres.
Thunder Wave (Lv 14) paralyses rather than injures, and Light Screen (Lv 51) is a protective barrier; both suit an animal that defends more than it hunts.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.
Mareep's lineage can carry Odor Sleuth as an egg move, a hint that smell matters to some lines, but it is not a natural move of Ampharos.

life_cycle.text: Mareep (0.6 m, 7.8 kg, four-legged) becomes Flaaffy at level 15 (0.8 m, 13.3 kg, upright) and Ampharos at level 30 (1.4 m, 61.5 kg, upright). The line stands up on two legs at the first evolution.
Mareep's fleece grows continually; it is shed completely in summer and grows back within a week.
The fleece is also insulation: it holds a lot of air, keeping Mareep cool in summer and warm in winter.
Read as development, the line moves from wool that makes charge (Mareep), to insulated skin that stores it at the cost of wool (Flaaffy), to a body whose output is mostly light (Ampharos).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Electric repertoire, all level-up: Thunder Shock (Lv 10), Thunder Wave (Lv 14), Charge (Lv 25), Discharge (Lv 34) and Thunder (Lv 68). Charge, which stores power for the next Electric move, is the build-up of static the entries describe.
Light: Signal Beam (Lv 42) and Power Gem (Lv 59) are both attacks of light, matching the beacon tail.
Only Ampharos learns Thunder Punch by level-up (Lv 30, on evolving), and it has Fire Punch at Lv 1; punches fit upright arms freed for striking. Flaaffy can only be taught them by a tutor.
Flash, the move that lights dark places in the field, is a machine move taught by people, not part of its wild repertoire.

ecology.text: If it grazes, it is a primary consumer of grassland (trophic level about 2); its diet is not recorded.
ecology.note: Follows from habitat and the juvenile's sheep-like build.

ecology.text: A bright light at night on open ground or a coast would attract night-flying insects and could make it conspicuous to predators; no entry mentions either.
ecology.note: A general consequence of carrying a light, not a described behaviour.

ecology.text: Mareep shares Johto's Route 43 with Girafarig and Pidgeotto, and Route 32 with Hoppip, Bellsprout and Wooper: open grassland and field-edge species.

humans.text: Its tail light acts as a beacon for lost people.
It has been treasured as a beacon since ancient times, and people in the old days used its light to send signals to others far away.
Signalling over long distance means people have kept and worked with Ampharos for a long time, more like a lighthouse keeper's animal than a pet.

homestead.text: Winter light: a bright, steady light source for the Glasshouse and the yard on long highland nights.
A beacon for anyone lost on the mountain or in the Ice Path approaches, which is the use people have always put it to.
Signalling between the homestead and outlying sites by light, as people did in the old days.
An electricity source: the line builds and stores charge, and Charge and Discharge are its own moves. Whether it can feed a battery or lamp steadily, and at what cost to the animal, is untested.
homestead.note: The capability records list this as gear (dynamo, lamps), not as anything an entry describes.

homestead.text: Mareep would give a wool crop: the fleece is shed fully every summer and regrows in a week. Shearing or gathering it means dealing with static, so handlers need insulated gloves.
Mareep's air-filled fleece is good insulation, so a flock could winter outdoors at Blackthorn better than most grassland species.

niche.foraging: not described; presumably grazing
niche.note: Diet is never stated. Mareep is on the tables by day and night; Ampharos's light is noted after dark.

relationships.note: People have treasured it as a beacon since ancient times; what the animal gains (shelter, food, protection) is not stated.
Route 43 with Mareep and Flaaffy, in Gold, Silver, HeartGold and SoulSilver.
Route 32 with Mareep, by day.

ecotypes.name: Stormfield flock
ecotypes.reading: Charge stores power for the next discharge, while Reflect and Safeguard shield the user and its companions from harm and from status effects. Together they suggest a lineage that holds a large charge and spends it protecting the group rather than attacking. Fits exposed upland pasture where a flock has no cover.
ecotypes.behavior: Bunches tightly when threatened, wool bristling with charge.

ecotypes.name: Dust-kicker
ecotypes.reading: Sand Attack throws grit into an attacker's eyes, and Take Down and Body Slam are full-weight rams. A lineage that defends on the ground, blinding and then barging. Fits dry, dusty steppe where static builds easily and soil is loose.
ecotypes.behavior: Kicks up dust, then charges with its head down.

ecotypes.name: Bleating sentinel
ecotypes.reading: Odor Sleuth is a sniffing-out move and Screech a piercing cry. A lineage that smells danger first and raises the alarm loudly. Fits grassland bordered by scrub or woods, where predators approach from cover.
ecotypes.behavior: Sniffs the wind often and screams at anything it can't see.

open_questions: What does any stage of the line eat?
Where do wild Ampharos live? None is wild in Gen I–IV, though 181.3 places some by the sea.
Is the line really absent from Crystal's wild, or is that a gap in the encounter data?
Does Ampharos keep any wool?
Do Ampharos use their lights to signal to each other, or only people use them that way?
How much electricity could one supply without harm, and how fast does it recharge?
Does Mareep shed its whole fleece in summer (179.2), or rely on it to keep cool (179.3)?

contradictions.note: Silver, FireRed and SoulSilver (179.2) say the fleece is fully shed in summer and regrows in a week; Crystal (179.3) says the air in the fleece keeps it cool in summer. If it is shed, it can't also be cooling the animal, unless the regrown week-old coat is what does the cooling.

Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald say it can be seen even from space; the Johto entries say from far away, or across the ocean at night. 'From space' reads as exaggeration, but it is stated as fact, not as a saying.

Arcanine.summary: Arcanine is a big, fast, fire-powered quadruped (1.9 m, 155 kg) of open grassland, admired since ancient times for its beauty, its grand mane and the way it runs, 'agilely as if on wings'. The fire blazing inside its body is its source of power, and its bark carries such majesty that anyone who hears it grovels. Much of what is written about it is legend: Chinese stories, and a claim that it can run over 6,200 miles in a day and night. It develops from Growlithe, a brave, loyal and fiercely territorial animal with a nose that never forgets a scent and can read the emotions of others. Arcanine forms only when a Growlithe is exposed to a Fire Stone, and none is wild in Gen I–IV.

anatomy.text: A large quadruped of 1.9 m and 155 kg, Fire type, with a grand mane.
The fire that blazes wildly within its body is its source of power.
It runs with great agility, as if on wings, and is known for its high speed.
Its category is 'Legendary Pokémon', though in game data it is an ordinary breeding species (Field group, catch rate 75), not a legendary.

diet.text: No entry for either stage says what the line eats.
Its wild moves are mostly bites (Bite, Fire Fang, Thunder Fang, and Crunch for Growlithe), which suggests a meat-eater, but that is a reading of moves.
diet.note: The machine reading's 'thermotroph' came from its Fire type alone.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat: grassland. An ancient picture scroll shows it running through prairies.
Arcanine is not found in the wild in any Gen I–IV game; it forms only when a Growlithe is given a Fire Stone.

Growlithe is a version exclusive: wild in Red, Yellow, Gold, Crystal, FireRed and HeartGold, but not Blue, Silver, LeafGreen or SoulSilver. In HeartGold it lives on Routes 36, 37 and 48 in Johto and 7 and 8 in Kanto; in the Kanto games also in the Pokémon Mansion.
In Sinnoh, Growlithe appears on Routes 201 and 202 only when FireRed is in the second slot.

behavior.text: A runner: speed is the thing it is most known for.
Its bark conveys majesty; anyone who hears it can't help but grovel.
Growlithe controls a big territory and defends it: it barks and bites to repel intruders, and roars loudly to drive out anything with an unknown smell.
Activity pattern is mixed in the data: Crystal lists Growlithe only in the morning and day, Gold at all times (more by day), and HeartGold's Route 48 at 20% by night.

social.text: No entry describes how Arcanine live with their own kind.
Growlithe is friendly, brave and trustworthy, and stands up fearlessly to bigger, stronger foes.
It is extremely loyal to its trainer: it barks at any opponent to protect them, and stays motionless until given an order.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, 75% male; slow growth.
Nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding, dens or care of young.

defense.text: Intimidation first: Intimidate lowers an opponent's attack, Roar (Lv 1) drives it off, and the canon bark makes listeners grovel.
Flash Fire turns fire aimed at it into extra power for its own fire attacks.
Growlithe defends with bark and bite.

senses.text: Growlithe has a superb sense of smell and never forgets a scent.
senses.analogy: Domestic dogs can be trained to follow one person's scent trail, a measure of how finely a carnivore's nose can separate individual odours.

senses.text: It uses its sense of smell to detect the emotions of other living things.
Odor Sleuth is a level-up move of both stages (Growlithe Lv 14, Arcanine Lv 1), so the adult keeps the nose.

life_cycle.text: Growlithe (0.7 m, 19 kg) becomes Arcanine (1.9 m, 155 kg) when exposed to a Fire Stone, about eight times heavier.

Stone evolution almost stops new natural moves: Arcanine's only level-up move after Lv 1 is Extreme Speed (Lv 39), while Growlithe keeps learning until Lv 48. Read biologically, the stone fixes the adult form at whatever stage it is applied.
Extreme Speed is the move form of the speed its entries are known for.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Arcanine's natural set is short: Bite, Fire Fang, Thunder Fang, Roar and Odor Sleuth at Lv 1, and Extreme Speed at Lv 39.

Growlithe's set is fuller: Ember, Flame Wheel, Fire Fang, Flamethrower, Heat Wave and Flare Blitz, with Helping Hand (Lv 17), a cooperative move, and Reversal (Lv 25), which hits hardest when the user is hurt, fitting an animal that stands up to bigger foes.
Strength, Dig and Rock Climb are machine moves taught by people.

ecology.text: Its role in a grassland community is unrecorded: no diet, prey or predators are named.
A large, territorial, fast-running animal of open country, it is likely to be near the top of whatever food web it lives in, if it hunts.
ecology.note: Hunting is not described for either stage.

humans.text: Admired for its beauty since ancient times: people are charmed by its grace when it runs, enchanted by its mane, and its proud, regal look has captured hearts for a long time.
An ancient picture scroll records people watching it run across prairies.
Growlithe is very friendly and faithful to people.

homestead.text: Guard and watch: the line holds territory, barks down intruders and roars at unknown smells, and the adult's bark makes listeners grovel.
Tracking: a nose that never forgets a scent could find lost people, animals or Pokémon on the mountain.
Reading visitors: it smells the emotions of others, which could give early warning of a frightened or hostile animal or person.
homestead.note: Canon says it can; whether it signals what it smells is untested.

homestead.text: A mount: 155 kg, fast, four-legged and obedient; carrying a rider is plausible, but no entry describes it.
homestead.note: The capability records list this from size and gear only.

homestead.text: Warmth: a body powered by an internal fire would be a living heater on cold nights; how hot its coat runs is not stated.
Needs: room to run, a territory it can patrol, and a fire-safe kennel away from hay and timber. Pair it with Blastoise as the fire crew.

niche.foraging: not described
niche.note: Diet is never stated. Activity data conflict between Crystal (day only) and HeartGold (night on Route 48).

relationships.note: Needed for Growlithe to become Arcanine.
Growlithe guards its trainer loyally; people have admired and kept the line since ancient times. What the animal gains is not stated.

ecotypes.name: Dawn howler
ecotypes.reading: Howl is a rallying cry that raises the user's strength, and Morning Sun restores it in sunlight. A lineage of open country that howls across a large territory at first light and recovers by basking. Fits wide, sunny prairies like the one on the ancient scroll.
ecotypes.behavior: Howls from a rise at dawn, then lies out in the early sun.

ecotypes.name: Grassfire driver
ecotypes.reading: Fire Spin traps a target in a ring of flame, Heat Wave sweeps a wide area, and Flare Blitz is a burning charge. A lineage that uses fire to herd and corner rather than just to strike. Fits dry grassland, and is the most dangerous to keep near people and crops.
ecotypes.behavior: Rings its quarry with fire, then charges.

ecotypes.name: Flock guardian
ecotypes.reading: Safeguard shields companions from status harm, Crunch is a crushing bite, and Body Slam pins with weight. A lineage that guards a group, holding intruders off with bite and bulk. Fits upland pasture with herds or flocks to protect, close to Growlithe's loyalty to its trainer.
ecotypes.behavior: Lies among the animals it guards and gets up only for intruders.

open_questions: What does the line eat?
Is it diurnal? Crystal says day only, HeartGold's Route 48 has it at night.
How fast can it really run, and for how long? '6,200 miles in a day and night' is folklore.
How hot is its body, and could it warm a room safely?
Does it signal the emotions it smells?
Why does a common, breeding species carry the category 'Legendary Pokémon'?

folklore.text: A legendary Pokémon in China, described in Chinese legends and considered magnificent.
It is said to be able to run over 6,200 miles (about 10,000 km) in a single day and night, and to race at unbelievable speed.
folklore.note: That would mean averaging over 400 km/h for 24 hours. Its high speed is canon (59.6); the figure is legend.

Beedrill.summary: The adult of the Weedle line: a large, fast, venomous insect with three poison stingers, one on each foreleg and the strongest on its tail. Beedrill is a hunter. It stings prey into submission and carries it back to its nest, defends that nest fiercely, and may attack in swarms; its favourite attack is a fast pass, striking with its needles and flying off. In SoulSilver it lives in Ilex Forest's rarer Headbutt trees, in the slot Butterfree fills in HeartGold, which swaps the forest's flower-visitor for a predator.

anatomy.text: A large flying insect (1.0 m, 29.5 kg) with three poisonous stingers: one on each foreleg and one on the tail.
anatomy.analogy: Real bees and wasps have a single sting at the tail, a modified egg-laying organ, which is why only females sting. Stingers on the forelegs have no real counterpart.

anatomy.text: The tail barb secretes the most powerful poison of the three.

diet.text: It hunts: it defeats prey with sharp, poisonous stings, then takes the victim back to its nest for food.
diet.analogy: Social wasps such as yellowjackets and hornets (Vespidae) kill or subdue insects and carry them back to the nest, where the prey is fed to the larvae.

diet.text: What it hunts isn't stated. 'It can take down any opponent' (15.3) is about fighting, not diet.
Its category is Poison Bee Pokémon, but nothing in its entries is bee-like in diet: no honey, nectar or flowers. Every feeding entry describes a hunter.

habitat.text: A forest animal with a nest it defends.

In SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's rare Headbutt trees (10%), Route 47's secret Headbutt trees, National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, and in Kanto on Route 2 (morning, plus a 4% night record) and in Viridian Forest. In HeartGold it appears only in the Contest.
Where the nest is, in a tree, on the ground or in a cavity, and what it is made of, isn't stated.

behavior.text: Extremely territorial around its nest: no one should ever approach it, for their own safety.
It flies at high, even violent, speed while stabbing; its best attack is to fly in, strike with its needles and fly off.
Mostly a morning and day animal by its SoulSilver grass records (Route 2, Viridian Forest), with one small night record on Route 2. Headbutt records have no time of day.

social.text: It sometimes attacks in swarms; angered, Beedrill attack in a furious swarm, and it may appear in one.
Swarming and a defended nest point to colonial life, but no entry describes a colony's size, a queen or any division of labour.
social.analogy: In real social wasps and bees, mass stinging in defence of the nest goes with colonies that have a reproductive queen and sterile workers.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio. Nothing in the Pokédex describes mating or eggs.
If the nest is a brood nest, the prey Beedrill carries home would feed young; but Weedle eat leaves under the leaves themselves, so the nest's part in breeding is unclear.
reproduction.note: No entry links the nest to eggs or young.

defense.text: Its stings are weapon and defence alike: it jabs an enemy repeatedly with its three stingers, and can take down any opponent with them.
Group defence: angered, they swarm.

Twineedle (Lv 16), Pin Missile (28) and Poison Jab (37) are the stingers in game form, Fury Attack (Lv 1) the repeated jabbing and Agility (31) its speed. Its ability, Swarm, powers up Bug moves in a pinch.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. A fast aerial hunter that defends a territory must find prey and spot intruders, but how is not described.

life_cycle.text: The adult of a larva-pupa-adult sequence: Weedle becomes Kakuna at level 7 and Kakuna becomes Beedrill at level 10.
The switch at metamorphosis is total: a leaf-eating larva becomes a hunting adult.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Pursuit (Lv 22), which hits a fleeing target harder, suits a hunter that gives chase; Focus Energy (13) and Assurance (34) concentrate its strikes.
Toxic Spikes (Lv 25) scatters poison barbs on the ground; in the wild it could be a way of making the approach to its nest dangerous.
moves_in_the_wild.note: A reading of the move; no entry describes barbs left around the nest.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Rage (19) and Endeavor (40) fit an animal that grows more dangerous when hurt or angered, as the swarm entries describe.

ecology.text: A predator at about trophic level 3, if, as seems likely, its prey are plant-eaters such as other insects.
In SoulSilver's Ilex Forest it holds Butterfree's Headbutt slot, so that version of the forest has a hunter where the other has a flower-visitor, and no described flower-visitor at all.
A territorial, swarming nest makes a patch of forest dangerous for other animals and people: an area it effectively controls.
At 1.0 m it is too big for Pineco to catch, though both live in the same rare Headbutt trees.

humans.text: Dangerous near its nest: the entries tell people to stay away, for their own safety.
No entry describes people keeping Beedrill or taking anything from it.

homestead.text: Its territoriality would defend a site, but it attacks anyone who comes near its nest, people included; the risk outweighs the guard.
Pest control: a hunter that carries prey home might take orchard and Glasshouse pests.
homestead.note: Untested: its prey is never named, and it might take more useful animals than pests.

homestead.text: No honey: unlike Butterfree, nothing in the record says Beedrill makes or stores any.
It needs a nest site it can defend and distance from people; keep it away from paths, the Glasshouse and the hatchery.

niche.foraging: fast aerial hunter: stings prey with forelegs and tail and carries it back to its nest

relationships.note: A slow, leaf-bound larva is the kind of prey a stinging hunter takes; they meet only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, since each is version-exclusive in Ilex Forest. Prey is never named.
Same rare Headbutt trees in SoulSilver's Ilex Forest.
Both hunt in Ilex Forest and share its rare Headbutt trees; Beedrill's records lean to day and Noctowl's to night, so any overlap in prey would be split by time.
Version counterparts in Ilex Forest; together only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest.

open_questions: What does it hunt?
What is the nest: where, of what, and how many Beedrill share it?
Who eats the prey it carries home, if Weedle eat leaves?
Is there a queen, or any division of labour within a swarm?
Does it take sugary food such as sap or nectar as well as prey?
Do both sexes sting?
The line has no HeartGold-SoulSilver egg moves, so no ecotypes can be read from breeding.

Blastoise.summary: Blastoise is a heavy, shelled water's-edge Pokémon (1.6 m, 85.5 kg) that carries pressurised water jets on its shell. It plants its feet before firing, and makes itself heavy on purpose to take the recoil; the jets hit harder than a fire hose, can punch through thick steel, and are accurate enough to knock a can over from 160 feet. In a pinch it withdraws into its shell or crushes an attacker under its weight. The line hunts from the water: Squirtle shoots water at prey and Wartortle hides in water to stalk it, and old Wartortle are known by the algae on their shells. No game in Gen I–IV has the line in the wild; every one is raised from a starter Squirtle.

anatomy.text: An upright, shelled body of 1.6 m and 85.5 kg, Water type.
Water spouts, described as rocket cannons, protrude from its shell and fire pressurised jets.
The jets are powerful enough to punch through thick steel and more forceful than a fire hose.
They are also precise: its water bullets can strike empty cans from over 160 feet (about 49 m).
In the juvenile the shell's rounded shape and surface grooves cut drag in water, so the shell is a swimming aid as well as armour.
Where the adult's water comes from (drawn in, stored, or made in the body) is not stated.

diet.text: A predator in its early stages: Squirtle shoots water at prey while in the water, and Wartortle hides in water to stalk unwary prey.
diet.analogy: Archerfish (Toxotes) knock insects off overhanging leaves with aimed jets of water spat from below the surface.

diet.text: No Blastoise entry mentions food; that the adult keeps hunting from the water is an inference from its line.
No prey is named for any stage.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: the water's edge.
It fires its jets with its feet planted on the ground, so it uses solid footing at the shore as well as the water.
Not found in the wild in any Gen I–IV game. Squirtle is a starter gift in Pallet Town (Red, Blue, FireRed, LeafGreen, and HeartGold and SoulSilver after beating Red) and in Vermilion City in Yellow.

behavior.text: Before shooting it plants its feet firmly, and it deliberately makes itself heavy so it can withstand the recoil of its jets.
How it makes itself heavy (taking on water, or some other means) isn't explained.
Older entries say the jets are used for high-speed tackles, which reads as jet propulsion.
Its activity pattern is unknown.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or territory for any stage.
The scratches on Wartortle's shell are evidence of its toughness as a fighter, which implies frequent fights, with rivals or predators.

reproduction.text: Monster and Water 1 egg groups, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male; the sex ratio is shared with the other starter lines and is probably a game convention.
Squirtle's shell is soft at birth; the back swells and hardens soon after into a resilient shell that prodding fingers bounce off.
reproduction.analogy: Hatchling turtles likewise start with a pliable shell that hardens as the bone beneath it ossifies.

defense.text: In a pinch it withdraws inside its shell; otherwise it crushes its foe under its heavy body.
The juvenile shelters in its shell and strikes back with water at every opportunity, drawing in its legs and spraying from its mouth.
Its wild repertoire backs this: Withdraw (Lv 10), Protect (Lv 24) and Iron Defense (Lv 46) for the shell, Rapid Spin (Lv 20) and Skull Bash (Lv 39) for the shell-first attack.
Torrent strengthens its Water moves when it is close to defeat.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Hitting a can at 160 feet implies good eyesight and fine aim.

life_cycle.text: Squirtle (0.5 m, 9 kg) becomes Wartortle at level 16 (1.0 m, 22.5 kg) and Blastoise at level 36 (1.6 m, 85.5 kg).
Wartortle balances while swimming fast by controlling its furry ears and tail.
Wartortle's age shows on its body: its thick tail fur deepens in colour with age, and algae on the shell mark a very old individual.
life_cycle.analogy: Algae commonly grow on the shells of freshwater turtles that bask little, such as snapping turtles.

life_cycle.text: Read as development, the water weapon moves from the mouth (Squirtle sprays water and foam) to the shell (Blastoise's cannons), and the animal shifts from a fast, drag-reducing swimmer to a heavy, planted gunner.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Water attacks by level-up: Bubble (Lv 7), Water Gun (Lv 13), Water Pulse (Lv 28), Aqua Tail (Lv 32) and Hydro Pump (Lv 60), the last matching the cannon entries.
Bite (Lv 16) is its only jaw attack, fitting a hunter that takes prey it has stunned with water.
Rain Dance (Lv 53) is a level-up move: a wild Blastoise could bring rain, which no entry mentions.
Surf, Waterfall, Strength and Rock Climb are machine moves, taught by people.

ecology.text: A predator of the water's edge, probably trophic level about 3 to 4, though its prey is never named.
Old individuals carry algae on their shells, so the line hosts at least one passenger community.

humans.text: Wartortle is very popular as a pet and is a recognised symbol of longevity, especially among older people.
When tapped, Wartortle pulls its head in but its tail still sticks out a little, a detail only someone handling one closely would note.
Blastoise is called brutal, and its jets can punch holes in steel, so it is dangerous at close range.

homestead.text: Fire crew: its jets hit harder than a fire hose and are accurate at 160 feet, which makes it the obvious partner for the homestead's fire-breathers.
Moving water for the Glasshouse or for washing down pens is plausible, but whether it can pump water from a tank or only from what it holds is not known.
homestead.note: The source of its water isn't stated.

homestead.text: Water crossings: Surf and Waterfall are taught moves, and at 1.6 m and 85.5 kg it can carry a rider on its shell.
Heavy work: it is heavy by design and learns Strength from a machine, so it can push or pull loads.
Needs a pond or river to swim and hunt in, and handlers who never stand in front of the cannons.

niche.foraging: juveniles shoot water at prey and stalk it from hiding in water; the adult's aimed jets suggest the same method at longer range

relationships.with: prey animals (not named in any entry)

relationships.note: Algae grow on the shells of very old Wartortle.

ecotypes.name: Silt-pond stalker
ecotypes.reading: Mud Sport and Muddy Water both cloud things with mud, and Foresight picks out what is hidden. A lineage of murky, still water that hides in its own silt and still finds its prey, the Wartortle habit of stalking from hiding taken further. Fits shallow, muddy ponds and marsh pools.
ecotypes.behavior: Stirs up the bottom, waits in the cloud, and strikes at what it can see but its prey can't.

ecotypes.name: Mist-lake elder
ecotypes.reading: Mist shrouds the user in fog, Aqua Ring wraps it in a veil of water that slowly heals, and Refresh clears poison, burns and paralysis. A lineage built for slow recovery and long life rather than fighting, which suits a line famous for longevity. Fits cold, misty highland lakes where individuals live long enough to grow algae on their shells.
ecotypes.behavior: Slow, rarely seen, and very old; heals rather than fights.

ecotypes.name: Jet charger
ecotypes.reading: Aqua Jet is a lunge so fast it is almost invisible, Water Spout is strongest when the user is unhurt, and Fake Out is a surprise opening blow. A lineage that opens every encounter with an overwhelming burst, the 'jets used for high-speed tackles' of 9.1 made central. Fits open, fast rivers where a fight is won in the first moment.
ecotypes.behavior: Hits first and hardest, then withdraws into its shell.

open_questions: Where does the water for its cannons come from: drawn in, stored, or produced?
How does it 'make itself heavy' to take the recoil?
Are the jets for propulsion, for shooting, or both? (see contradictions)
What does the line eat?
How long does the line really live? Old Wartortle grow algae; 'ten thousand years' is folklore.
Where do wild Squirtle, Wartortle and Blastoise live? None is wild in Gen I–IV.

contradictions.note: Red, Blue and LeafGreen (9.1, 9.9) say the jets are used for high-speed tackles, which suggests propulsion; Crystal (9.5) has it planting its feet to fire them, and Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald (9.6, 9.7) describe them as precise ranged weapons. Both uses are possible, but the entries describe different animals in action.

folklore.text: Wartortle is said to live 10,000 years.
folklore.note: Line folklore. Its reputation for longevity is canon (8.3); the figure is not.

Butterfree.summary: The adult of the Caterpie line, and the only member of the Ilex Forest community whose entries describe it visiting flowers. Butterfree flies from flower to flower collecting honey, which it rubs onto the hairs of its legs and carries back to a nest; it can find flowers in bloom a long way off, by some entries more than six miles. A powder on its wings sheds rain, so it forages even in the heaviest downpours, and in a fight the same dust is toxic. In HeartGold it lives in Ilex Forest's rarer Headbutt trees.

anatomy.text: A large flying insect (1.1 m, 32.0 kg) whose wings are covered in powder or dust.
The wing powder does two jobs: it repels water and it is poisonous.
anatomy.analogy: The 'dust' on real butterfly and moth wings is overlapping scales (Lepidoptera means 'scale-winged'), and the scales make the wings strongly water-repellent. Real wing scales are not poisonous.

anatomy.text: Its legs carry hairs onto which it rubs honey to carry it.
anatomy.analogy: Bees carry pollen packed onto the hind legs (in honeybees and bumblebees, a 'pollen basket') and carry nectar inside the body in the crop; honey on leg hairs is closer to how bees carry pollen than to how any insect carries nectar.

anatomy.text: Its ability is Compound Eyes (its accuracy is boosted); no entry describes the eyes themselves.

diet.text: It feeds on honey from flowers. It loves it, collects it every day, and flits from flower to flower gathering it.
The entries say honey, not nectar. Flowers yield nectar; honey in the ordinary sense is nectar concentrated and stored. Butterfree may be making honey in its nest from the nectar it collects.
diet.note: A reading of the word; no entry describes what happens in the nest.
diet.analogy: Honeybees make honey in the hive by evaporating nectar and adding enzymes to it.

diet.text: A central-place forager: it carries what it collects back to a nest rather than eating everything where it finds it.
It ranges widely: it can find, extract and carry home honey from flowers blooming over six miles (about 10 km) from its nest.
diet.analogy: Honeybees usually forage within a few kilometres of the hive, though flights of nearly 10 km have been recorded; six miles is at the far end of what real bees do.

habitat.text: A forest animal by Gen 3 habitat. In HeartGold it is in Ilex Forest's rare Headbutt trees (10%), Route 47's secret Headbutt trees, National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, and in Kanto on Route 2 and in Viridian Forest. In SoulSilver it appears only in the Contest, and Beedrill holds its Ilex Forest slot.
It forages wherever flowers bloom, but its records are in trees and woodland, so its nest is probably in or among trees.

behavior.text: It collects honey every day and in all weather: its water-repellent wings let it fly and forage even in the heaviest rain.
Day-active: its HeartGold grass records (Route 2, Viridian Forest) are in the morning and by day only. Its Headbutt records have no time of day, and no entry states its activity.

social.text: It has a nest, but no entry says whether the nest is shared or how many Butterfree use it.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio. As the line's adult it is the breeding stage, but nothing is said about mating, eggs, or whether the nest has anything to do with young.
Captivate (Lv 36), a move that works only on the opposite sex, is the one hint of courtship display in its repertoire.
reproduction.note: A reading of a level-up move; no entry describes courtship.

defense.text: In a fight it beats its wings at high speed to release highly toxic dust into the air.
Poison Powder, Stun Spore and Sleep Powder (all Lv 12) are that dust in game form, with three different effects.
Flight is its other defence, with wing-driven moves for driving attackers off: Gust (16), Whirlwind (22), Silver Wind (28).

senses.text: It can identify flowers in bloom at a distance, has a superior ability to search out honey, and can locate flower patches with only tiny amounts of pollen.
Which sense does this isn't stated. Compound Eyes suggests sight; detecting tiny amounts of pollen suggests smell.
senses.analogy: Real butterflies find flowers by sight, including colours in the ultraviolet that people can't see, and by scent picked up on the antennae.

life_cycle.text: The adult of a larva-pupa-adult sequence: Caterpie becomes Metapod at level 7 and Metapod becomes Butterfree at level 10.
Metamorphosis changes its diet and its range: Caterpie chews leaves in the foliage, while Butterfree drinks from flowers across miles of country and carries food to a nest.
life_cycle.analogy: Separate larval and adult niches are the usual pattern in insects with complete metamorphosis, and are thought to spare young and adults from competing for the same food.

moves_in_the_wild.text: No move is about feeding. Its level-up moves are defence (the three powders), flight (Gust, Whirlwind, Silver Wind, Tailwind, Bug Buzz) and psychic attack (Confusion from evolution, Psybeam at 24).
Supersonic (Lv 18) is a sound attack and Safeguard (Lv 34) protects against status conditions; nothing in the entries corresponds to either.
The line has no HeartGold-SoulSilver egg moves.

ecology.text: Probably the forest's main pollinator: it goes from flower to flower and seeks out pollen, which would carry pollen between flowers. No entry actually says it pollinates.
ecology.analogy: Flower-visiting insects pollinate incidentally: pollen sticks to their bodies as they feed and rubs off at the next flower.

ecology.text: A primary consumer (trophic level 2) that takes a reward plants offer, nectar, rather than plant tissue.
By carrying food from flowers up to six miles away back to a nest in the forest, it brings energy into the forest from well outside it.
In SoulSilver's Ilex Forest its Headbutt slot goes to Beedrill, a hunter, so that version of the forest has no described flower-visitor at all.
At 1.1 m it is too big for Pineco to catch; its likely predators are larger birds, and its toxic dust is its answer to them.
ecology.note: No predator of Butterfree is named.

humans.text: The capability records already link it to food, hauling, scouting, plant care and air travel from these same entries; no entry says people take its honey.
Its dust is toxic, so people should keep clear of a Butterfree that is fighting.

homestead.text: Honey: a Butterfree brings honey back to its nest every day, so a Butterfree nesting at the homestead might yield a harvest, if no more is taken than it needs.
homestead.note: Nobody has described taking honey from a Butterfree nest, or how much one stores.

homestead.text: Pollination for the orchard and the Glasshouse Berry rows, if Berry plants need pollinators at all, which no source says.
homestead.note: Rests on the inferred pollinator role.

homestead.text: A flower scout: it finds flowering patches miles away, which would tell a forager where things are in bloom.
homestead.note: Untested: no one has followed a Butterfree to its flowers.

homestead.text: Rain doesn't stop it, which suits a wet highland; cold is another matter, since all its HeartGold records are lowland.
It needs flowers within reach, a sheltered nest site in trees, and handlers who stay out of its wing dust.

microhabitat: flower patches up to about 10 km out
niche.foraging: central-place forager: flies flower to flower collecting honey and carries it home to a nest on its leg hairs

relationships.note: Honey from flowers; the entries' word is honey.
Visits flower after flower and seeks out pollen; no entry says it carries pollen.

Budew opens its bud in the sun to release pollen; Butterfree seeks out patches with tiny amounts of pollen. Budew is in Ilex Forest only when the Sinnoh Sound plays on the radio, and no entry links them.
Same rare Headbutt table in Ilex Forest.
Same rare Headbutt trees; Noctowl hunts at night, when a day-active Butterfree would be resting. Its toxic dust argues against it being easy prey.
Version counterparts in Ilex Forest; together only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest.

open_questions: What is the nest: where, of what, shared or solitary, and is it where eggs are laid?
What is the honey for? It is gathered daily and carried home, but Caterpie eat leaves, so it isn't food for the young unless the young are fed something else.
Does it pollinate? It visits flower after flower, but no entry says it carries pollen.
Does it eat pollen as well as honey?
Which sense finds flowers six miles away?
Can it survive highland winters, or would Blackthorn be a summer-only range?
The line has no HeartGold-SoulSilver egg moves, so no ecotypes can be read from breeding.

Caterpie.summary: The leaf-eating larva of Butterfree. Caterpie climbs trees on sticky feet, eats leaves bigger than itself, hides among foliage of its own green, and when its red feeler is touched it releases a foul smell. It grows by moulting several times, then covers itself in silk and becomes Metapod. In HeartGold it is the animal most often met in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning and by day, and it is never met there at night; in SoulSilver, Weedle takes its place slot for slot.

anatomy.text: A small green larva (0.3 m, 2.9 kg) with a red feeler, or antenna, on top of its head.
Its short feet end in suction pads or cups that stick to any surface, so it can climb slopes, walls and trees without tiring.
anatomy.analogy: Real caterpillars grip with prolegs, fleshy legs on the abdomen ringed with tiny hooks (crochets), rather than with suction.

anatomy.text: The red feeler is where its defensive stench comes from (see Defence). No entry says whether it is also a sense organ.

diet.text: It eats leaves, voraciously: it can eat a leaf bigger than its own body while you watch.
It climbs trees to forage, so it feeds in the foliage of trees and shrubs, not only near the ground.
No entry names its food plants. HeartGold puts it both in Ilex Forest's grass and in its Headbutt trees, so tree leaves are the likeliest food.

habitat.text: A forest animal of foliage and trees.

In HeartGold it is in Ilex Forest's grass (60% of encounters by day, 50% in the morning, none at night) and its common Headbutt trees (30%), on Routes 30 and 31, in National Park, and in Kanto on Route 2 and in Viridian Forest.

In SoulSilver it is absent from Ilex Forest and the routes and appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest in National Park, where Weedle also appears. Caterpie and Weedle are version counterparts that hold identical slots at identical rates.
Its microhabitat is foliage in the understory and lower canopy, where its colour matches the leaves.

behavior.text: Day-active. In HeartGold's tables it appears in the morning and by day and never at night, in Ilex Forest and on every route where it occurs. This rests only on the time-of-day split in the encounter tables.
Its day is climbing and eating; 'tirelessly' and 'tenaciously' are the entries' words for the climbing.
Where it spends the night isn't recorded. Its Headbutt-tree records (which have no time of day) and its leaf camouflage suggest it stays in the foliage.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or any dealings with its own kind.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing in the Pokédex describes eggs or where they are laid; breeding belongs to the adult, Butterfree.
Eggs are probably laid on or near the plants the larva eats, since a hatchling that can only crawl has to start close to food.
reproduction.analogy: Female butterflies lay on the larval food plant, often after testing it with taste receptors on their feet.

defense.text: When its feeler is touched, or to drive enemies away, it releases a horrible stench from the feeler or antennae on its head.
defense.analogy: Swallowtail caterpillars (Papilionidae) have an osmeterium, a forked organ behind the head that they turn out when disturbed, releasing a strong-smelling defensive secretion. Caterpie's red feeler matches it closely.

defense.text: Camouflage: it crawls into foliage that is the same colour as its body.
defense.analogy: Crypsis, blending into the background, is one of the commonest defences of real caterpillars.

defense.text: Shield Dust (it blocks the added effects of attacks taken) is its ability, and String Shot (Lv 1) lets it slow an attacker with silk.
It has enemies to drive away, but no entry names them; the forest's birds are the obvious candidates (see Relationships).

senses.text: Nothing is said directly about its senses. It finds leaves, climbs to them and reacts to touch on its feeler, which is as much as the entries imply.

life_cycle.text: It grows by moulting repeatedly, shedding its green skin each time.
life_cycle.analogy: Larval growth in stages (instars) separated by moults; most real caterpillars pass through about five.

life_cycle.text: At the last moult it covers itself with silk and becomes a cocoon, Metapod. In the games this happens at level 7, and Metapod becomes Butterfree at level 10.
life_cycle.analogy: Complete metamorphosis (holometaboly): larva, pupa, adult. Real butterflies usually pupate as a bare chrysalis hung from a silk pad; spinning a full silk cocoon is mostly a moth habit.

life_cycle.text: Caterpie is the line's feeding stage: the pupa doesn't feed and the adult lives on honey, so almost all the leaf-eating in the Butterfree line is done by Caterpie.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Tackle and String Shot are its moves from hatching. Bug Bite comes at level 15, but it becomes Metapod at 7, so a wild Caterpie rarely if ever has it: its working toolkit is pushing and silk.
String Shot is the game form of its silk, which it uses for its cocoon. Using silk as a safety line or to tangle attackers is a reading of the move, not something the entries say.
moves_in_the_wild.note: Only the cocoon use is canon.

moves_in_the_wild.text: The line has no egg moves in HeartGold and SoulSilver, so breeding gives no basis for distinct Caterpie lineages.

ecology.text: A primary consumer of foliage (trophic level 2), and in HeartGold the leaf-eater most often met on Ilex Forest's floor by day.
Its stench and camouflage are anti-predator defences aimed at hunters that find prey by sight. In Ilex Forest the Headbutt-tree birds, Hoothoot and Noctowl, are the plausible predators.
ecology.note: No entry names a predator of Caterpie.

ecology.text: It turns leaves into the forest's flower-visitor: everything Butterfree is built from was eaten by Caterpie.
It shares the forest grass with Oddish in shifts: Caterpie in the morning and by day, Oddish only at night.

humans.text: Easy to catch (catch rate 255) and common on Johto's first routes; National Park's Bug-Catching Contest includes it in both versions. No entry describes people using it.
Anyone handling one should leave the feeler alone: touching it sets off the stench.

homestead.text: Silk. Caterpie makes silk for its cocoon, and cocoons left behind once Butterfree has emerged could be gathered and spun without harming anything.
homestead.note: Untested: nothing describes how much silk a cocoon holds or what it is like.
homestead.analogy: Eri silk (from Samia ricini) is spun from cocoons after the moth has left, unlike mulberry silk, which is reeled from cocoons whose pupae are killed first.

homestead.text: In a garden it is a pest, not a helper: it eats a lot of leaves. Keep it away from crops and the Glasshouse Berry plants.
Small enough to live indoors (0.3 m, 2.9 kg), but handle it gently: a touch on the feeler sets off the stench.
Whether it can get through a Blackthorn winter is unknown: all its Johto records are lowland forest and routes.

niche.foraging: climbs into foliage and chews leaves, morning and day

relationships.note: Both larvae eat leaves in the same forest. The games never let them share Ilex Forest in one version and give each the other's slots at the same rates; read as competitive exclusion that is a hypothesis resting on a version-exclusive design device.
Together only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, in both versions.

Both are in Ilex Forest's common Headbutt trees; Hoothoot (0.7 m, 21.2 kg) is large enough to take a 0.3 m larva. Against it: Hoothoot's grass records are all at night and Caterpie's all by day, so they would meet only at dawn or with the larva resting in foliage; Hoothoot's diet is not stated.
Noctowl catches prey in darkness and is in Ilex Forest's rare Headbutt trees; a larva resting in foliage at night is within reach. Prey is never named.
Carnivine (the 'Bug Catcher Pokémon') hangs from branches to ambush prey; it is in Ilex Forest only when the Sinnoh Sound plays on the radio.
Same grass, opposite shifts: Caterpie morning and day, Oddish night only.

open_questions: Which plants does it eat? No entry names one.
What eats it? Its defences imply predators that hunt by sight, but none is named.
Where does it spend the night? It drops out of the walking tables after dark.
How long is the larval stage in real time? Level 7 says nothing about days.
Does its silk have any use besides the cocoon, and is it worth gathering?
The line has no egg moves in HeartGold and SoulSilver, so no ecotypes can be read from breeding; are there regional differences anyway?

contradictions.text: One feeler or two? Yellow, Gold, Ruby/Sapphire and Diamond/Pearl/Platinum (10.2, 10.3, 10.6, 10.9) describe a single feeler or antenna; Emerald and HeartGold (10.7, 10.10) say antennae.
contradictions.note: A forked organ, like a real swallowtail caterpillar's osmeterium, could be described either way.

Charizard.summary: Charizard is a winged, fire-breathing mountain Pokémon: 1.7 m and 90.5 kg, able to fly to nearly 4,600 feet and breathe fire hot enough to melt boulders. It flies about looking for strong opponents and never turns its fire on one weaker than itself, though its flames can start forest fires by accident. Its tail flame, which in Charmander is a measure of its life, flares whitish-blue when it is furious. Every Charizard in Gen I–IV is raised from a Charmander given to a trainer; the line's wild home is described only as the rocky mountains where Charmeleon's tails shine at night like stars.

anatomy.text: An upright, winged, tailed body of 1.7 m and 90.5 kg, Fire and Flying type.
Wings strong enough to carry it high, close to 4,600 feet (about 1,400 m).
A flame burns at the tip of its tail; it burns more intensely when Charizard breathes out a blast of fire, and flares whitish-blue or light blue when it is furious.
It breathes or spits fire hot enough to melt boulders, or almost anything.
In the juvenile, the tail flame burns from birth and reflects its health; Charmander's life would end if the flame went out.

diet.text: No entry for any stage says what the line eats.
Charmander prefers hot places and hot things, but that is a preference for heat, not a diet; the machine reading's 'thermotroph' came from its Fire type alone.
Charmeleon knocks foes down with its tail and tears them up with its claws, which describes fighting, not necessarily feeding.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: mountain. Charmeleon live in rocky mountains, where their fiery tails shine at night like stars.
It ranges into forest as well: its flames are known to cause forest fires.
Not found in the wild in any Gen I–IV game. Charmander is a starter gift in Pallet Town (Red, Blue, FireRed, LeafGreen, and HeartGold and SoulSilver after beating Red) and on Route 24 in Yellow.

behavior.text: It flies about in search of strong opponents.
It never turns its fiery breath on an opponent weaker than itself.
This is a change from the middle stage: Charmeleon is hotheaded, constantly seeks opponents, and calms down only when it wins, with no mention of sparing the weak.
Its activity pattern is unknown. Charmeleon's tails are seen shining at night, which shows they are out at night, not necessarily active.

social.text: No entry describes Charizard living in groups or pairs.
Seeking strong opponents while sparing weak ones suggests contests with rivals of similar strength, as ritual or status contests rather than predation.
Charmeleon's tails shining 'like stars' in the rocky mountains implies many individuals within sight of each other at night.
