behavior.text: Swinub regularly turns up hot springs while foraging.
Activity is uncertain: Crystal puts Swinub in the Ice Path by day and morning only, with Delibird in its slot at night; HeartGold, SoulSilver, Gold and Silver have it at all hours.

social.text: No entry describes herds, pairs or interaction with its own kind.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, even sex ratio, 20 egg cycles, slow growth. Nothing is said about breeding or young.

defense.text: Size, ice tusks and a charging habit: Piloswine charges repeatedly at whatever is in front of it, hackles up.
Thick, shaggy hair protects against cold, at the cost of sight.
Snow Cloak (harder to hit in hail) or Oblivious (can't be infatuated) are its abilities; Mist and Endure are among its own moves.

senses.text: Smell is the line's main sense: Swinub's nose is very sensitive and finds food and hot springs under ice; Piloswine, which can't see, checks its surroundings with its nose.
Piloswine is also very sensitive to sound.
Odor Sleuth is a Lv 1 move at every stage, the games' version of the nose.

life_cycle.text: Swinub (0.4 m, 6.5 kg) becomes Piloswine at level 33 (1.1 m, 55.8 kg), and Piloswine becomes Mamoswine (2.5 m, 291.0 kg) when it levels up knowing Ancient Power.
Piloswine has Ancient Power at Lv 1 in HeartGold, and Swinub can carry it as an egg move or learn it from a tutor, so the trigger is available several ways.
Development adds hair, tusks and size: a small rooting pig, a blind shaggy charger with ice tusks, then a giant with impressive ice tusks.
An 'ancient' move as the trigger for an ice-age form reads like a lineage recovering an ancestral body plan.
life_cycle.note: A reading of a game mechanic; no entry describes the evolution.

life_cycle.text: A frozen Mamoswine was dug up from 10,000-year-old ground and woke up, to much amazement.
life_cycle.analogy: Frozen mammoth carcasses are recovered from Siberian permafrost, but no animal that size could revive. Microscopic bdelloid rotifers have been revived from Siberian permafrost about 24,000 years old.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Ground and mud moves suit a rooter: Mud Sport, Mud-Slap, Mud Bomb and, later, Earthquake (Lv 40).
Ice moves come from the line itself: Powder Snow, Hail (Lv 25, Mamoswine), Ice Fang, Mist and Blizzard.
Take Down (Lv 32) is Piloswine's repeated charge in move form; Double Hit (Lv 33, Mamoswine only) fits two tusks.
Strength and Rock Smash, behind its hauling and clearing records, are machine moves.

ecology.text: A rooting fungivore and frugivore when young (trophic level about 2): it turns over soil and dead grass for mushrooms and berries.
Rooting disturbs ground cover and soil, and Swinub's habit of uncovering hot springs could open new warm, wet patches for other species.
ecology.note: Plausible engineering effect; the entries describe finding hot springs, not their effect on the community.

ecology.text: A relict: a species past its peak, surviving where the cold persists.
In HeartGold's Ice Path, Swinub shares every floor with Golbat, Zubat and Jynx; in Crystal, Delibird takes Swinub's slot at night.

humans.text: People have dug frozen Mamoswine out of ancient ice and soil.
Swinub's nose finds things people want: mushrooms, berries and hot springs.

homestead.text: A local animal: Swinub is common in the Ice Path next door, and the line is built for exactly Blackthorn's cold.
Finding hot springs: Swinub turns them up while foraging, even under ice, which could locate geothermal water and heat for the estate.
A winter forager: its nose finds mushrooms and berries under ice and dead grass, useful for the kitchen and for surveying the woods.
Heavy winter hauling: a 291 kg, four-legged animal that grips icy ground with rugged hooves (in Piloswine). The capability record lists harness and saddle.
Work Piloswine quietly and give it room: it can't see, is very sensitive to sound, and charges repeatedly at what it can't identify.
Keep it cool: the line declined when the climate warmed. A sheltered, cold summer range matters more than a warm winter barn.
Swinub will dash off after any good smell; fence the kitchen garden and the berry beds.

niche.foraging: roots with snout and tusks for mushrooms, berries and food buried under ice, guided by smell
niche.note: Swinub's diet; Mamoswine's own diet is never stated. Activity: all hours in HeartGold, day and morning only in Crystal.

relationships.with: mushrooms that grow under dead grass

relationships.note: It finds them; whether it uses them is not said.
Its tusks thicken with snow; its population depends on ice.
Crystal's Ice Path: Swinub by day and morning, Delibird in the same slot at night.
Ice Path, every floor, in Crystal and HeartGold/SoulSilver.

ecotypes.name: Glacier relict
ecotypes.reading: The most Mamoswine-like Swinub: Icicle Spear fires icicles in a volley, the tusks-of-ice canon in move form, and Ancient Power is the very move a Piloswine needs to evolve. A lineage that carries its own evolution trigger from the egg. Fits permanent ice, the habitat its ancestors thrived in.
ecotypes.behavior: Grows into a Mamoswine without help; keeps to the coldest ground.

ecotypes.name: Moraine rammer
ecotypes.reading: Piloswine's charging made heavier: Double-Edge and Body Slam are full-weight hits, and Rock Slide brings down stones. A lineage of rocky glacial debris where a charge sends rock tumbling. Fits moraine slopes and scree below ice fields.
ecotypes.behavior: Charges harder and more often; loose rock comes down behind it.

ecotypes.name: Frost-ground breaker
ecotypes.reading: A digger for the hardest ground: Fissure splits the earth, Mud Shot throws wet soil, and Curse makes it slower but stronger and tougher. A lineage that breaks frozen soil to reach buried food, building on Swinub's frozen-ground nose. Fits permafrost tundra where food lies under a hard crust.
ecotypes.behavior: Slow, methodical, leaves cracked and turned ground behind it.

open_questions: What does Mamoswine eat?
Are the tusks grown, or built up from ice (221.7 says they thicken when it snows)?
Do they live in herds? No entry says.
How large is the Ice Path Swinub population, and does it ever reach Piloswine or Mamoswine there?
Was the frozen Mamoswine found in soil (473.2) or ice (473.3)? And how did it survive?
Does Swinub use the hot springs it finds, or only find them?
Is Swinub diurnal (Crystal) or active at all hours (HeartGold)?

contradictions.text: Where the frozen Mamoswine was found: soil dating back 10,000 years (Platinum) or ice dating back 10,000 years (HeartGold).
Piloswine's sight: its hair 'obscures' its sight in Gold and HeartGold; it is 'unable to see' in Diamond and Pearl.
contradictions.note: Degree, not kind.

Meganium.summary: A large, sun-loving Grass Pokémon whose main tool is chemistry. The ring of petals around Meganium's neck gives off a scent that calms aggression, and in a fight it releases more of it to take the fight out of its opponent. Silver, SoulSilver and the Sinnoh Pokédex add that its breath can bring dead plants back to health. No entry says what it eats, and no game puts it in the wild: every Meganium starts as a Chikorita handed to a new trainer.

anatomy.text: A heavy quadruped (1.8 m, 100.5 kg) with a ring of flower petals around its neck; the flower is the source of its scent.
Its breath carries something that restores dead or dying plants, so the active substance is exhaled as well as given off by the flower.
Two separate chemical outputs are described: a calming aroma from the petals and a plant-restoring breath. Whether they are the same substance is not said.

diet.text: No Pokédex entry for any stage says what this line eats.
The line probably gains some energy from sunlight: Chikorita loves to bask and sunbathe, and Synthesis, which restores health in sunlight, is a level-up move from Lv 12.
A 100 kg animal that walks about is unlikely to run on sunlight alone, so it probably also eats; grazing on plants is the obvious guess for a grassland Grass type, but nothing says so.
diet.note: An energy-budget argument, not evidence. The diet is genuinely missing.
diet.analogy: Real animals that photosynthesise are almost unknown. The nearest case is kleptoplasty in sacoglossan sea slugs such as Elysia chlorotica, which keep chloroplasts from the algae they eat; even there, how much energy photosynthesis supplies is debated.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex lists it under grassland.
It is not found in the wild in any Gen I-IV game. Chikorita is a starter gift in New Bark Town in Gold, Silver, Crystal, HeartGold and SoulSilver, and a gift in Littleroot Town in Emerald.
The 'sunny forest' in the Crystal entry is a simile for how standing next to it feels, not a statement about where it lives.

behavior.text: The line is docile and loves to soak up the sun; Chikorita uses the leaf on its head to find warm places to bask.
Sunbathing suggests a day-active animal, at least in the young; no entry for Meganium itself gives an activity pattern.
Its response to a threat is to calm it: in battle it gives off more of its scent to blunt the opponent's fighting spirit.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups, pairs or how it treats its own kind.
Its scent works on other animals, so it communicates, or at least acts, chemically at close range: anyone standing beside it is refreshed.

reproduction.text: Monster and Grass egg groups, 20 egg cycles, and 87.5% male (the ratio the games give most starter lines). Nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding, eggs or care of young.
Bayleef carries a small tree shoot inside each curled leaf around its neck. Whether these shoots have any reproductive role, like buds or cuttings, is not said.
reproduction.note: Raised only because a shoot is the part of a plant that can grow on its own; no entry links the shoots to breeding.

defense.text: Chemical pacification rather than flight or armour: the flower's scent soothes, and it releases more in a fight. Chikorita does the same, waving its leaf to keep a foe back while the leaf's sweet scent calms everyone nearby.

Its level-up moves fit a defensive animal: Poison Powder (a chemical deterrent), Reflect, Light Screen and Safeguard (protective screens), and Sweet Scent, which in the games lowers the opponent's evasion and draws wild Pokémon in.
Overgrow, its only ability, strengthens its Grass moves when it is badly hurt.

senses.text: Chikorita's head leaf senses temperature and humidity, and it uses it to seek out warm places.
Whether Meganium keeps this sense once the head leaf is no longer prominent is not said.

life_cycle.text: Chikorita (0.9 m, 6.4 kg) becomes Bayleef at level 16 (1.2 m, 15.8 kg) and Meganium at level 32 (1.8 m, 100.5 kg). Most of the growth is in the last stage: about six times the mass for half again the height.

The scent organ moves and develops: a single leaf on Chikorita's head, then a ring of curled, tubular leaves around Bayleef's neck, each holding a small tree shoot, described in Diamond and Pearl as buds; then Meganium's ring of petals.
The simplest reading is that Bayleef's ring of buds opens into Meganium's flower.

The scent's effect changes with stage: Chikorita's is sweet and calming, Bayleef's is spicy and stimulating (it makes people peppy, restores health, and one entry says sniffing it makes you want to fight), and Meganium's calms again.

moves_in_the_wild.text: No wild Meganium exists in the games, so the level-up list is the species' own repertoire rather than anything observed. It is weighted to plant chemistry and self-care: Razor Leaf and Magical Leaf for attack, Poison Powder and Sweet Scent for scent and powder, Synthesis for sunlight, and Petal Dance, learned on evolving at Lv 32, using the new petals.
Aromatherapy (level-up, Lv 60) cures the status problems of the whole party, which matches the canon of a scent that refreshes everyone nearby.
Body Slam (Lv 46) is the only heavy physical move it learns by itself, and it fits the adult's mass.

ecology.text: If its breath restores plants in the wild, a Meganium would speed regrowth of damaged vegetation around it, acting as a facilitator for the plant community.
Its calming scent could lower aggression among animals sharing its patch, changing how the community behaves rather than its numbers.
ecology.note: The entries describe the effect on people and on opponents in battle, not on a wild community.

ecology.text: Its trophic position is unknown because its diet is.

humans.text: Its line reaches people as a starter: Chikorita is given out in New Bark Town to new trainers in every Johto game.
People benefit from the scents directly: standing beside Meganium is refreshing, and Bayleef's aroma perks people up.

homestead.text: Plant care in the Glasshouse and the orchard: its breath restores dead or failing plants. How large an area it can treat, and how often, is untested.
A calming presence for the nursery, the clinic or a tense pen: its petal aroma calms aggressive feelings.
Field healing: Aromatherapy, which it learns on its own, cures status problems across the party.
What it needs: sunlight and somewhere warm. Chikorita actively seeks warm places, so a Blackthorn winter probably means indoor time in the Glasshouse.
Keep Bayleef apart from animals that are already agitated: one entry says its spicy scent makes you want to fight.
Its size puts it in the carrying-a-rider range, but no entry says it carries people; Strength and Rock Smash would be taught moves, not its own.

niche.foraging: unknown; probably part sunlight (basking, Synthesis) and part feeding, but no entry says what it eats
niche.note: The machine reading's 'phototroph' comes from the Grass type alone. Trophic level is left null because the diet is unknown.

relationships.note: Restoring plants changes the habitat others use; the scale in the wild is unknown.

ecotypes.name: Rooted meadow
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that settles: Ingrain anchors it and draws health from the ground, and Leech Seed drains whatever stays near it. Together they make a sit-and-drain animal that holds one patch instead of roaming. Fits damp lowland meadow with deep soil.
ecotypes.behavior: Picks a spot, roots, and lets rivals weaken; rarely moves once settled.
ecotypes.analogy: Mistletoes (Viscum) are hemiparasites: they photosynthesise but take water and minerals from a host, which is roughly what Leech Seed on top of Synthesis would look like.

ecotypes.name: Lullaby grazer
ecotypes.reading: The calming-scent canon pushed further: Grass Whistle puts an opponent to sleep with a tune, and Aromatherapy keeps its own group free of status problems. A lineage that ends fights before they start. Fits open grassland crowded with other grazers.
ecotypes.behavior: Answers a threat with song and scent rather than a charge; tolerant of close neighbours.

ecotypes.name: Vine wrestler
ecotypes.reading: A physical lineage: vines to lash and grip, Wring Out to squeeze (strongest against a healthy opponent), Counter to return a blow, and Body Slam for the adult's weight. Fits brushy edges and thickets where predators come close before they are seen.
ecotypes.behavior: Grapples rather than calms; a Meganium that holds its ground.

open_questions: What does it eat? No entry for any stage says, and a 100 kg animal is unlikely to live on sunlight alone.
Is the plant-restoring substance in its breath the same as the calming aroma from its petals?
Why does Bayleef's scent stimulate (153.1-153.6) when Chikorita's and Meganium's calm?
What are the tree shoots inside Bayleef's neck leaves for, and what becomes of them in Meganium?
Does Meganium keep Chikorita's sense of temperature and humidity?
Is there a wild population anywhere? The games only ever give it out as a starter.

Metapod.summary: The pupa of the Butterfree line: a hardened green shell, nearly motionless, inside which Caterpie's body is rebuilt into Butterfree. It doesn't eat and can do little but harden its shell further; the body inside is soft and tender, and a large enough knock can pop it out of the shell. Its whole strategy is to stay still, armoured and out of the way. In HeartGold it is met in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning and by day and in the common Headbutt trees, a stage that lasts, in the games, from level 7 to level 10.

anatomy.text: A green shell (0.7 m, 9.9 kg) around a soft, weak, tender body.
Once set, the shell is described as hard as an iron slab, or steel-hard; while it is still soft the tender body is exposed and vulnerable.

By game size the pupa is heavier and more than twice as long as the larva (9.9 kg against Caterpie's 2.9 kg, 0.7 against 0.3 m), though it hasn't eaten in between. A non-feeding pupa can't gain mass, so the stage sizes are best read as stylised.

diet.text: It doesn't feed. No entry mentions food, and every entry has it motionless inside its shell, preparing to evolve.
diet.analogy: Real insect pupae do not feed; they live on reserves laid down by the larva.

diet.text: Everything it uses to build the adult must come from what Caterpie ate.

habitat.text: A forest animal. In HeartGold it is in Ilex Forest's grass (30% of encounters in the morning and by day, none at night) and common Headbutt trees (10%), on Routes 30 and 31, in National Park, in Route 47's secret Headbutt trees, and in Kanto on Route 2 and in Viridian Forest. In SoulSilver it appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest.
Being met in the grass suggests many Metapod pupate low, in understory vegetation; the Headbutt records show others up in trees.

behavior.text: Motionless: it stays still in its shell and hardly moves, because it is preparing its soft insides for evolution.
It quietly endures hardships while it waits.

The time-of-day split in its tables (morning and day only) can't be activity, since a pupa does nothing at any hour. It probably mirrors where and when Caterpie pupates, or how findable pupae are; it is unexplained.

social.text: Nothing is said about other Metapod or any other animal.

reproduction.text: In the games Metapod is in the Bug egg group (15 egg cycles) and can breed.
Biologically a pupa is not a reproductive stage; breeding Metapod is best read as a game convention rather than part of its natural history.

defense.text: Its only active defence is to harden its shell, and it stays motionless to avoid drawing attack.
The shell has limits: the tender body inside can't withstand a harsh attack, and a large impact can pop it out of the shell.
Harden (Lv 1, again at Lv 7) is its entire level-up repertoire; its ability, Shed Skin, may heal its own status problems.
Being green like Caterpie, it is probably hidden among leaves as well as armoured.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: Metapod is the pupa between Caterpie and Butterfree: Caterpie sheds its skin, covers itself with silk and becomes a cocoon, and Metapod becomes Butterfree at level 10. Crystal calls this stage its 'pre-evolved form'.
Inside, the body is soft and is being prepared for evolution while the shell is hardened as much as possible.
life_cycle.analogy: Complete metamorphosis: inside a real pupa much of the larval body is broken down and the adult is built from small clusters of cells (imaginal discs) carried over from the larva.

life_cycle.text: Whether the hard shell is hardened silk (the cocoon of 10.8) or the pupa's own skin beneath it isn't stated.
In game terms the stage lasts three levels, 7 to 10, the shortest in the line.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Harden is all a wild Metapod does, which matches every entry.
Its tutor moves (String Shot, Iron Defense, Bug Bite) are taught by people and say nothing about the wild animal.

ecology.text: A non-feeding stage: it takes nothing from the forest, and is a store of energy that predators might take.
For anything able to break or prise open the shell it is a large, immobile parcel of food; its defence is being hard and hidden, not being inedible.
ecology.note: No entry names a predator.

ecology.text: How many pupae survive sets how many Butterfree reach the flowers, so this stage links the forest's leaf-eating to its flower-visiting.

humans.text: Trainers mostly meet it as a stage to get through on the way to Butterfree at level 10. No entry describes people using it.

homestead.text: It needs a quiet, sheltered, undisturbed spot, ideally among foliage, and protection from knocks, which can pop it out of its shell.
Empty shells or cocoon silk left after Butterfree emerges could be collected as a material.

niche.foraging: none: a non-feeding pupa living on reserves from the larva
niche.note: No feeding guild applies. Trophic level 2 is its position as food: its body is built from Caterpie's leaf-eating.

relationships.note: Same grass and the same common Headbutt trees in HeartGold's Ilex Forest; it is Caterpie's next stage.
Version counterparts in Ilex Forest; together only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest.
Both are in Ilex Forest's common Headbutt trees and Hoothoot pecks (Peck, Lv 9); whether a peck gets through an iron-hard shell is doubtful. No predator of Metapod is named.

open_questions: Is the hard shell hardened silk or the pupa's own skin?
How long is the pupal stage in real time?
What, if anything, preys on pupae? None is named.
Why is it absent from the night tables when it can't move?
What happens to a Metapod knocked out of its shell (11.2): can it survive, or finish developing?
Why does the pupa outweigh the larva by more than three times without feeding?
The line has no HeartGold-SoulSilver egg moves, so no ecotypes can be read from breeding.

contradictions.text: How protective is the shell? Ruby/Sapphire, Emerald and Diamond/Pearl/Platinum make it iron- or steel-hard (11.6, 11.7, 11.9); Yellow and FireRed say a large impact can pop it out and it can't withstand a harsh attack (11.2, 11.8).
contradictions.note: Probably both true: a hard shell with fragile contents. Recorded because the entries differ in how safe they make it sound.

Milotic.summary: Milotic is a 6.2 m serpentine Pokémon of the bottoms of large lakes, famous above all for its looks: its scales shift through rainbow colours with the angle of view, and it has been painted and sculpted for generations. It can calm anger and hostility; Sapphire says its body glows vivid pink and sends out a pulsing wave that soothes restless spirits, and several games repeat the saying that one glimpse of it ends a quarrel. It develops from Feebas, a ragged, ignored, hardy fish that eats anything and schools in weedy ponds and rivers, and in Gen III–IV only a Feebas whose beauty has been raised becomes Milotic. No Milotic is wild in these games.

anatomy.text: A long, serpentine body of 6.2 m and 162 kg, Water type.
Its scales are described as rainbow-coloured and change colour with the viewing angle.
anatomy.analogy: This is iridescence, a structural colour, as in many fish scales and the wings of Morpho butterflies, where microscopic layers rather than pigments reflect different colours at different angles.

anatomy.text: Its body can glow vivid pink.
Marvel Scale toughens it when it is suffering a status condition, the game's version of its scales as armour.
Feebas, by contrast, has ragged, tattered fins from the start of its life.

diet.text: No Milotic entry says what it eats.
Feebas eats anything, which lets it live even in polluted streams and lakes.
Whether the adult keeps the juvenile's eat-anything habit is not stated; a 162 kg lake-bottom animal must eat a good deal of something.

habitat.text: It lives at the bottom of large lakes.
Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the line: the water's edge.
Feebas is far more flexible: it can live in the sea and in rivers, in weed-choked ponds, in polluted water, and on little water at all; HeartGold and SoulSilver put it at the bottom of rivers.

Milotic is not wild in any Gen I–IV game. Feebas is fished only from a few particular water tiles: on Hoenn's Route 119 in Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald, and in Mt. Coronet's basement in Diamond, Pearl and Platinum. It is absent from Johto and Kanto.
That mechanic matches the Pokédex: Feebas are populous but cluster in set locations.

behavior.text: When its body glows vivid pink, it releases a pulsing wave of energy that brings calm to restless spirits.
It has the power to calm anger and hostility and to settle bitter feuds.
Its activity pattern and daily routine are unknown.

social.text: No entry describes how Milotic live with their own kind.
Feebas forms schools at the bottom of rivers.
An animal whose main stated power is to end conflict may live where conflict is costly, among many others in a crowded lake, but this is a reading, not a record.
social.note: The entries describe its effect on people and 'restless spirits', not on its own kind.

reproduction.text: Water 1 and Dragon egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio; its eggs hatch as Feebas.
Nothing describes courtship, spawning or care of young.

defense.text: Its defence seems to be pacification: those who see it are calmed, and its pulsing wave soothes restless spirits.
Its wild repertoire is unusually restorative: Refresh (Lv 9), Recover (Lv 21), Safeguard (Lv 45) and Aqua Ring (Lv 49) all heal or protect.
Wrap (Lv 1), a constricting hold, suits a 6 m serpentine body.
Feebas has no real defence: slow and dim-witted, it is an easy catch, and survives by being hardy and ignored.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: Feebas (0.6 m, 7.4 kg, fish-shaped) becomes Milotic (6.2 m, 162 kg, serpentine): ten times the length and more than twenty times the mass in one step.

In Gen III–IV the change needs a Feebas with high beauty, a condition these games raise by feeding it Pokéblocks or Poffins. Read biologically, Milotic forms only from a Feebas that someone has fed and cared for.
life_cycle.note: The beauty mechanic is general game knowledge, not stated in the pack.

life_cycle.text: The pack also lists a trade while holding a Prism Scale. That item comes from later games and does not exist in Gen III–IV, so it should not count for these games.
life_cycle.note: Outside knowledge, flagged for checking against the data.

life_cycle.text: Its growth rate is erratic: slow at first, then very fast.
Feebas's only level-up moves are Splash, Tackle and Flail; the juvenile has almost no repertoire, and nearly everything Milotic does arrives with the change.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Water: Water Gun (Lv 1), Water Pulse (Lv 13), Aqua Tail (Lv 29) and Hydro Pump (Lv 37); Twister (Lv 17) reflects its Dragon egg group.
Attraction: Captivate (Lv 25) and Attract (Lv 41) are the move forms of a beauty that disarms.
Rain Dance (Lv 33) is a level-up move, so a wild Milotic could bring rain, which no entry mentions.

ecology.text: Its role in a lake community is unrecorded: no diet, prey or predators are named for the adult.
Feebas, eating anything and tolerating polluted water, is a hardy generalist that can occupy waters most species avoid.

humans.text: It is called the world's most beautiful Pokémon and features in many works of art, including paintings and statues.
It is breathtakingly beautiful.
Feebas is the opposite: ridiculed for its shabby looks, ignored by researchers, and raised by few trainers.

homestead.text: A calming presence: it can calm anger and hostility, which makes it a candidate for anywhere tempers run high, people's or animals'.
Water travel on a large lake: at 6.2 m it is big enough to carry a rider, and Surf is a taught move.
Its pink glow could serve as a faint light near water, but nothing says it is bright or steady.
homestead.note: The capability records list light from this entry.

homestead.text: It needs a large, deep lake; a 6 m animal that lives on the bottom cannot be kept in a pond.
Feebas is easy to keep: it eats anything, tolerates poor water and survives on little of it, so a weedy pond would do. Turning one into Milotic takes a deliberate feeding regime.

microhabitat: weedy ponds, river bottoms, even polluted water (Feebas)
niche.foraging: not described for the adult; Feebas eats anything
niche.note: Guild and trophic level come from Feebas's 'eats anything'; the adult's diet is never stated.

relationships.note: Feebas's habitat.
It calms quarrelling people; what it gains, if anything, is unknown. 350.5's 'rises from the lake when people bicker' is folklore.

ecotypes.name: Deepwater lantern
ecotypes.reading: Confuse Ray is a dazzling light that confuses, Hypnosis lulls to sleep, and Light Screen is a shield of light. With the pink glow of 350.2, the set suggests a lineage that works with light in the dark: dazzling, lulling and shielding at depth. Fits deep, dark lake bottoms.
ecotypes.behavior: Glows in the depths; whatever comes close becomes drowsy and confused.

ecotypes.name: Fog-lake peacemaker
ecotypes.reading: Mist shrouds the user in a protective fog, and Haze wipes out every stat change on the field, read here as damping down a fight for everyone in it. A lineage whose calming is built into its repertoire as well as its looks. Fits cold, often-misty mountain lakes.
ecotypes.behavior: Rises in the fog when the water is disturbed, and the disturbance stops.

ecotypes.name: Weedbed dweller
ecotypes.reading: Mud Sport coats the user in mud, and Tickle lowers a foe's guard by distraction. A lineage that keeps to the muddy, weed-choked shallows of Feebas's youth rather than moving to deep lakes. Fits small, weedy, eutrophic ponds.
ecotypes.behavior: Stays in the weeds and mud where it hatched; rarely seen in open water.

open_questions: What does Milotic eat?
How does it calm others: by being seen (350.4, 350.8), or by a pulsing wave of energy (350.2)?
Is the lake-bottom habitat fact (350.2) or saying (350.3)?
Could a Feebas become Milotic in the wild, without anyone raising its beauty?
Does the pink glow give usable light?
How long does it live, and how does it breed?

contradictions.note: Sapphire (350.2) gives a physical mechanism: a pulsing wave of energy when its body glows pink. FireRed, LeafGreen, HeartGold and SoulSilver (350.4, 350.8) say the sight of it does it, but only as a saying. Ruby (350.1) just calls it a power.
Sapphire (350.2) states that Milotic live at the bottom of large lakes; Emerald (350.3) says only that it is said to.
Pearl (350.6) states it is the world's most beautiful Pokémon; Ruby and Emerald (350.1, 350.3) report it as what is said or considered.

folklore.text: It is said to be the most beautiful of all Pokémon.
Those who see it are said to forget their will to fight, and a glimpse of it is said to calm any hostile feeling.
When people bicker, it is said to rise from the depths of lakes to calm violent hearts.
It is said to live at the bottom of large lakes.
folklore.note: Sapphire (350.2) states this as fact.

Miltank.summary: Miltank is an all-female grassland Pokémon, and almost everything the Pokédex says about it concerns its milk. It gives over five gallons a day, sweet enough for children and nourishing enough to be called the ultimate drink for the sick or weary, and the milk grows richer after it has a calf or when babies are near. Nothing in canon says what it eats, how it lives with its own kind, or how a species with no males breeds. In Johto it grazes the same routes as Tauros, an all-male species of the same egg group, though no entry links the two.

anatomy.text: A compact, upright body with a tail: 1.2 m and 75.5 kg, Normal type, with udders.
Thick Fat makes it more resistant to Fire and Ice attacks, which points to a heavy layer of insulating fat.
Milk output of over five gallons a day (about 19 litres) from a 75.5 kg animal is a quarter of its body weight every day, so its mammary tissue and its food intake must both be enormous for its size.
anatomy.analogy: A high-yielding dairy cow gives roughly 25–35 litres a day from a body of 600 kg or more, a far smaller share of its weight.

diet.text: No entry says what Miltank eats.
Its grassland habitat and cow-like build suggest a grazer, and its milk output implies it eats a great deal; neither is stated.
diet.note: The machine reading's 'herbivore' came from its Normal type alone, which says nothing about diet.

diet.text: Milk Drink (level-up, Lv 11) has it drink its own milk to recover, so the milk is food for Miltank too, not only for its young.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat: grassland.
In Johto it is on Routes 38 and 39 in every game (5%, walking), and in HeartGold and SoulSilver also on Route 47 (20%), a route whose surf and fishing tables put it beside the sea.

Elsewhere it is hard to find: in Emerald only in the Safari Zone's northern expansion, and in Diamond, Pearl and Platinum only with the Poké Radar on Routes 209 and 210. Pearl has it far more often on the Radar (20%) than Diamond (2%).
It is absent from the Kanto games (FireRed, LeafGreen) and from Ruby and Sapphire.

behavior.text: Activity pattern is unclear. Gold and Silver list it on Routes 38 and 39 in the morning, day and night alike; Crystal lists it only in the morning and day; HeartGold and SoulSilver don't split by time.
Gold and Silver's Route 38 table also carries a swarm-condition slot for it at the same 5%, which looks like a quirk of the data rather than a real outbreak.
No entry describes its daily life beyond milk production.

social.text: Nothing is said about herds, pairs or hierarchy.
Its milk becomes richer when it is around babies, not only its own, which suggests it responds to any young nearby and could nurse young that aren't its own.

reproduction.text: All Miltank are female (0% male); Field egg group, 20 egg cycles.
In the games it breeds with a male of any Field-group species, or with Ditto, and the egg always hatches as Miltank.

A biological reading: Miltank needs a male of another species to start an egg but passes on only its own inheritance. Tauros, all male, Field group, and found on the same routes, is the obvious partner.
reproduction.note: No entry pairs Miltank with Tauros or describes how it breeds.
reproduction.analogy: The Amazon molly (Poecilia formosa) is an all-female fish whose eggs must be triggered by sperm from males of related species, yet the young inherit no genes from the father.

reproduction.text: After it has given birth, its milk carries much more nutrition than usual.
reproduction.analogy: Colostrum, the first milk a cow gives after calving, is much richer in protein and antibodies than later milk.

defense.text: No entry mentions predators or how it defends itself.

Its level-up repertoire is heavy-bodied: Defense Curl (Lv 5) then Rollout (Lv 19), Stomp (Lv 8), Body Slam (Lv 24) and Gyro Ball (Lv 41). Read together, it curls and rolls into attackers or tramples them.
Scrappy lets its attacks hit Ghost types, and Thick Fat blunts fire and ice; both are game abilities without a Pokédex explanation.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Detecting babies nearby, which changes its milk (241.7), implies it can sense young by sight, sound or smell, but the cue isn't named.

life_cycle.text: Miltank doesn't evolve and has no pre-evolution; its growth rate is slow.
What its calves look like, how long they nurse and when they mature is not described.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Healing: Milk Drink (Lv 11) restores its own health, and Heal Bell (Lv 48) is a soothing chime that clears status conditions from it and its allies. Both are level-up moves, so a wild Miltank carries them.
Heal Bell working on allies fits a herd animal that tends others, but no entry describes it doing so.
moves_in_the_wild.note: A reading of a move's effect, not a behaviour anyone has described.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Growl (Lv 3), Captivate (Lv 35) and Wake-Up Slap (Lv 55) round out the set; Zen Headbutt (Lv 29) is a head strike.

ecology.text: Most likely a large grazer of grassland (trophic level about 2), and so a consumer of grass and forbs on the routes it lives on; its diet is not stated.
ecology.note: Follows from habitat and build, not from any entry.

ecology.text: If it nurses young other than its own, its milk would be a resource for the whole grassland nursery, not just its calf.
ecology.note: An extension of 241.7.

humans.text: Its milk is highly nutritious, the ultimate drink for the sick or weary.
It gives over five gallons a day of sweet milk that children and adults both enjoy; people who can't drink milk make it into yogurt.
Milking it takes skill: a knack for pulling rhythmically on the udders.
Every one of its entries is about its milk and how people use it, which implies a long history of being kept and milked; no entry describes a wild Miltank's life.

homestead.text: A dairy animal: over five gallons of milk a day, which can be drunk or made into yogurt, so one Miltank could supply a household and more.
The homestead's infirmary drink: its milk is the ultimate beverage for the sick or weary, and Milk Drink and Heal Bell are its own healing moves.
Thick Fat suggests it can stand Blackthorn's highland winters better than most grassland animals.
It needs a person with the knack for milking, every day: an animal giving this much milk must be milked regularly, and what happens if it isn't is not recorded.
It needs pasture or fodder in quantity, but since its diet is unknown, what to feed it is the first thing to find out.
Strength and Rock Smash are taught moves it can learn, so it could pull or clear stone on demand, though nothing in canon presents it as a draught animal.

niche.foraging: not described; presumably grazing
niche.note: Diet is never stated; guild and trophic level follow from habitat and build.

relationships.note: Same walking tables on Routes 38 and 39 in Gold, Silver, Crystal, HeartGold and SoulSilver (both day and morning only in Crystal). Tauros is all male, Miltank all female, both Field egg group; no entry connects them.
Route 47 in HeartGold and SoulSilver, where Ditto is common (41%). Ditto is the other partner Miltank can breed with in the games.
Its diet is not stated.

ecotypes.name: Crèche keeper
ecotypes.reading: Helping Hand boosts an ally, Present hands something over, and Psych Up takes on another's state. Together they suggest a lineage built around care in groups: provisioning and supporting young and herd-mates, the milk's response to any nearby baby carried further. Fits settled herds on rich lowland pasture.
ecotypes.behavior: Nurses and guards whatever young are near, its own or not.

ecotypes.name: Pasture brawler
ecotypes.reading: Hammer Arm and Seismic Toss are grappling, throwing attacks, and Reversal hits harder the more hurt the user is. A lineage that turns and fights rather than rolling away, heaving an attacker off the ground and fighting hardest when wounded. Fits open country with predators and no cover to flee to.
ecotypes.behavior: Stands over its calf and throws whatever comes close.

ecotypes.name: Snowfield sleeper
ecotypes.reading: Curse (for a non-Ghost) slows the user while making it tougher, Endure survives a blow that should fell it, and Sleep Talk acts while asleep. With Thick Fat, the combination suggests a lineage that rides out hard seasons by slowing down and resting a great deal. Fits high, cold pasture with long winters, such as the Blackthorn highlands.
ecotypes.behavior: Slow and heavy in winter, dozing through storms but never quite off guard.

open_questions: What does Miltank eat, and how much? Over five gallons of milk a day needs a large intake.
How does an all-female species breed in the wild? Is Tauros the partner, as shared routes and egg group suggest?
Does its milk change when its own calf is born (241.2), or when any baby is near (241.7), or both?
Does it nurse young that aren't its own?
Is it active at night? Gold and Silver say yes, Crystal says no.
What happens to a Miltank that isn't milked, or whose calf is weaned?
Does it live in herds?

contradictions.note: Silver and FireRed (241.2) say the milk is richer when it has just had a baby; SoulSilver (241.7), rewriting the same entry, says when it is around babies. One is a physiological change after birth, the other a response to young nearby. Both may be true.

folklore.text: Children who drink Miltank's milk are said to grow up into hearty, healthy adults.
folklore.note: Reported belief; its nutritional value is canon (241.1), the long-term effect is not.

Noctowl.summary: The adult of Hoothoot and Ilex Forest's night hunter. Noctowl's eyes concentrate faint light so it can see in near darkness, and its soft feathers make no sound in flight, so it reaches prey unheard; the entries say it never fails to catch prey in the dark. When it thinks hard it turns its head 180 degrees, or upside down. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Ilex Forest's rarer Headbutt trees, and it is the community's best candidate for a top predator.

anatomy.text: A large owl (1.6 m, 40.8 kg).
Specially adapted eyes that concentrate even faint light.
anatomy.analogy: Owls' large, tube-shaped eyes are packed with rod cells, and many owls hunt in very dim light.

anatomy.text: Extremely soft, supple feathers that make no sound in flight.
anatomy.analogy: Real owl flight feathers have comb-like serrations on the leading edge and a soft, velvety surface, both of which reduce flight noise.

anatomy.text: It can rotate its head 180 degrees, and flip it upside down.
anatomy.analogy: Real owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees, which they need because their eyes barely move in their sockets.

diet.text: A predator: it sneaks silently up on prey and never fails to catch prey in darkness.
Its prey is never named.
In Ilex Forest the night animals within reach are Oddish, Zubat and Paras in the grass, larvae and pupae resting in the trees, and Magikarp splashing at the pond surface.
diet.note: Rests on shared habitat, activity and size; none of these is named as its prey.

habitat.text: A forest animal. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's rare Headbutt trees (10%) and Viridian Forest's, and in grass at night on Routes 2, 8, 13 to 15, 43 and 47.
Its nearest record to Blackthorn is Route 43, at night.

behavior.text: A night hunter: its entries are about catching prey in darkness, and every grass record of it in HeartGold and SoulSilver is at night.
When it needs to think it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellect; flipping its head upside down is a sign of very complex thinking.
It stalks: it sneaks up on prey without being detected.

social.text: Nothing is said about pairs, groups or territories.

reproduction.text: Flying egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio. Nothing in the Pokédex describes nesting or young.

defense.text: No entry describes a defence. Its size probably suffices in Ilex Forest, where only Golduck is larger.
Its abilities are Insomnia (it can't be put to sleep) and Keen Eye (its accuracy can't be lowered); Hypnosis and Reflect are among its moves.

senses.text: Superior night vision: it can pick out objects with the tiniest amount of light and see clearly in murky darkness.
The entries credit its hunting to vision and silent wings; hearing is never mentioned.
senses.analogy: Many owls find prey by sound as well as sight; barn owls can catch prey in total darkness by hearing alone.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Hoothoot at level 20. Hoothoot's entries are about timekeeping and Noctowl's about hunting; the time-sensing organ isn't mentioned again.
Its egg moves sit with Hoothoot, the line's first stage; the ecotypes below use them.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Sky Attack (Lv 1), a powerful strike after a charge-up, fits a hunter that drops onto prey from a perch; Peck, Take Down and Air Slash are its other attacks.
Hypnosis followed by Dream Eater (57) is a game combination: put the target to sleep, then drain it. Hunting by putting prey to sleep is a reading, not canon.
moves_in_the_wild.note: No entry describes Noctowl using sleep on prey.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its psychic moves (Confusion 22, Zen Headbutt 37, Extrasensory 42) go with the entries about its intellect.

ecology.text: Probably Ilex Forest's top predator at night (trophic level about 3.2): a large hunter that never misses in the dark, in a forest whose night animals are small (Oddish 0.5 m, Paras 0.3 m, Zubat 0.8 m).
ecology.note: Its prey is unnamed; the trophic level assumes a mix of plant-eaters and smaller predators.

ecology.text: It is on the rare Headbutt table at 10%, as a top predator might be, though a table rate isn't abundance.
Bird Pokémon peck Pineco by mistake; Noctowl is one of two birds in Ilex Forest that could.

humans.text: No entry describes its dealings with people.
The capability records list it under light and night travel from 164.1. Night travel fits; light is a misreading, since it concentrates light rather than making it.

homestead.text: Night watch: it sees in near darkness and moves silently, so a resident Noctowl would see intruders, predators and strays after dark.
homestead.note: Untested; depends on it staying near the homestead.

homestead.text: It might keep small crop-raiding animals away at night, but it may take small Pokémon as readily.
homestead.note: Its prey is unnamed.

homestead.text: Protect small or sleeping residents, and eggs, at night if a Noctowl hunts nearby.
Route 43 is its nearest wild home; it needs tall trees or high perches and a dark day roost.

microhabitat: forest clearings and grass at night
niche.foraging: silent, vision-guided stalking and capture of prey in darkness

relationships.note: Oddish is the night animal most often met in Ilex Forest's grass and is a third of Noctowl's height. Against it: Oddish is poisonous and armed with powders.
Both active at night in Ilex Forest; Zubat flies in colonies and is fast.
relationships.analogy: Real owls take bats occasionally, though bats are a small part of their diet.

relationships.note: In the night grass; its spores (Effect Spore) would make it a costly catch.
A day-active larva resting in foliage at night; HeartGold only.
As for Caterpie, SoulSilver only; its warning colours and barb argue against.
Magikarp's pointless jumping makes it easy for predators like Pidgeotto to catch mid-jump; an owl hunting the pond edge could do the same.
relationships.analogy: Fish-eating owls are real: Blakiston's fish owl (Bubo blakistoni) takes fish from rivers in the Russian Far East and Hokkaido.

relationships.note: Attempted only: birds peck Pineco by mistake and its shell protects it.
Same rare Headbutt trees, same nights; the size difference may split their prey.

ecotypes.name: Dive hunter
ecotypes.reading: A lineage built for fast, powerful strikes from height. Fits open country and forest edges where prey is spotted from tall perches and the approach is long.
ecotypes.behavior: Hunts from high perches over clearings rather than inside the forest.

ecotypes.name: Shadow stalker
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that pushes further into darkness and strikes where the prey can't see it coming. Fits dense, old forest like Ilex.
ecotypes.behavior: Hunts the darkest hours under the thickest canopy.

ecotypes.name: Flusher
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that drives prey out of cover with wind and sound before striking. Fits grassland and reedbeds where prey hides low.
ecotypes.behavior: Beats and calls over cover, then pounces on whatever bolts.

open_questions: What does it eat?
Does it hunt by hearing as well as sight?
Does it keep Hoothoot's clock?
What is the head-turning for: is it really about thinking (164.2, 164.7), or about seeing?
Does it try to eat Pineco, and does the explosion deter it?
Does it fish?

Oddish.summary: A walking weed. By day Oddish plants itself in fertile ground, face buried and only its leaves showing, and takes up nutrients from the soil through its whole body; at night moonlight wakes it, and it walks off on its root-feet, scattering seeds as it goes. It is Ilex Forest's night shift: in HeartGold and SoulSilver it is the animal most often met in the forest's grass after dark, and it is never met there by day. Pull one up and it shrieks.

anatomy.text: A small, plant-like animal (0.5 m, 5.4 kg): a body topped with leaves, walking on two root-like feet.
While it is planted by day, its feet are thought to change shape and become like the roots of trees.
The more fertile the soil, the glossier its leaves become.

diet.text: By day it buries itself in soil and absorbs nutrients from the ground through its entire body.
It looks for fertile, nutrient-rich soil before planting itself.
It grows by absorbing moonlight, or 'bathing' in it.
If it runs on light at all, the leaves it keeps above ground by day (43.8) may catch sunlight too, which would fit its Grass type and its ability, Chlorophyll (faster in sunshine).
diet.note: Crystal says it stays underground to avoid the sun (43.5), which cuts against this.
diet.analogy: Full moonlight is several hundred thousand times dimmer than direct sunlight, far too little to drive photosynthesis in real plants.

diet.text: Absorb (Lv 1) and Mega Drain (21) take energy from another organism and are part of its wild repertoire, but no entry says Oddish feeds that way.

habitat.text: Grassland by Gen 3 habitat. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's grass at night (60%), on Routes 5, 6, 24 and 25 at night, and in the Johto Safari Zone at night.
By day it stays quietly underground, in the cold ground, out of the sun.
Its microhabitat is the fertile soil of the forest floor and its clearings: soil it chooses by day, the grass above it at night.

behavior.text: Nocturnal: moonlight wakes it, and it roams actively at night; by day it keeps its face buried and stays quietly underground. HeartGold and SoulSilver meet it in grass only at night.
It roams far and wide at night.
It alternates between a rooted, plant-like day and a mobile night.

social.text: Nothing is said about other Oddish. Its evolved form Bellossom gathers in groups to dance (182.1), but that is the adult, and a different branch of the line.

reproduction.text: It sows seeds as it walks about at night.

In the games it breeds from eggs (Grass egg group, 20 egg cycles). How the seeds relate to the eggs isn't explained: whether a seed grows into an Oddish, an ordinary plant or something else is unknown.

defense.text: By day it buries itself with only its leaves showing, to avoid detection by its enemies, and it can be mistaken for a clump of weeds.
If anyone tries to pull it out of the ground, it shrieks horribly.
defense.analogy: A parallel in folklore rather than biology: the European legend of the mandrake (Mandragora), whose root was said to scream when pulled from the ground.

defense.text: Acid (9), Poison Powder (13), Stun Spore (15) and Sleep Powder (17): a small animal well armed with chemicals.

senses.text: It responds to moonlight: exposure to it starts it moving.
It seeks out fertile soil, so it can sense soil quality somehow; how is not described.

life_cycle.text: Oddish becomes Gloom at level 21; Gloom becomes Vileplume with a Leaf Stone or Bellossom with a Sun Stone.

The line turns carnivorous as it develops: Gloom's sweet, sticky nectar is used to attract prey, and Vileplume lures prey with its huge petals, doses them with toxic spores and eats them. Oddish itself is never described eating animals.
The Sun Stone branch reverses the night habit: Bellossom closes its petals and sleeps at night and dances in sunshine.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Sweet Scent (Lv 5) is a lure. In Gloom the lure is for prey (44.1); in Oddish it might draw animals that carry its seeds, but that is a reading.
Moonlight (Lv 33) heals by moonlight, matching the entries, but Oddish evolves at 21, so a wild Oddish almost never has it.
Its wild repertoire before evolving is drain (Absorb), acid (Acid) and powders (Poison Powder, Stun Spore, Sleep Powder).

ecology.text: A producer, or as near as any regular member of the community comes to one: it draws nutrients from soil and energy from moonlight, which puts it at trophic level 1.
It disperses its own seeds by walking, far and wide each night, spreading its kind across the forest floor.
Digging in by day may loosen and mix the soil, and it selects fertile patches, but nothing says whether it depletes or enriches them.
ecology.note: Untested.

ecology.text: It shares Ilex Forest's grass with the caterpillars in shifts: the larvae in the morning and by day, Oddish at night.

humans.text: People can take it for a clump of weeds and try to pull it up, which sets off its shriek.
FireRed gives it a scientific name, 'Oddium Wanderus', in the same entry as the hearsay about how far it walks (see Folklore).
The capability records list it under light from Gold's 'moon light'. That is a misreading: moonlight wakes it, it doesn't make light.

homestead.text: A night gardener of sorts: it seeks fertile soil, plants itself, and sows seeds wherever it walks. An Oddish loose in the Glasshouse at night would seed its own kind among the Berry rows.
homestead.note: What its seeds grow into is unknown.

homestead.text: A soil test on legs: its leaves grow glossier the more fertile the soil, so a planted Oddish would show where the ground is good.
homestead.note: One entry; untested.

homestead.text: It needs soft, fertile soil to bury itself in by day, darkness and moonlight at night, and cool ground out of the sun.
It chooses the cold underground (43.5), so Blackthorn's cool soils may suit it, though no record puts it in the highlands.
homestead.note: The capability records already file this under cold tolerance; that rests on one entry.

niche.foraging: plants itself in fertile soil by day and absorbs nutrients through its body; absorbs moonlight at night while walking and sowing seeds
niche.note: It takes up soil nutrients as a plant does; the guild names its energy source.

relationships.note: Noctowl catches prey in darkness, and Oddish is the night animal most often met in Ilex Forest's grass (0.5 m against Noctowl's 1.6 m). Against it: Oddish is poisonous and armed with powders, and the enemies it hides from (43.8) are daytime ones.
Hoothoot's grass records are at night, as Oddish's are. Its diet is not stated.
Both draw on what's below ground: Oddish takes soil nutrients, Paras sucks tree roots. Whether they compete for the same nutrients is untested.
Oddish, Zubat and Paras make up the whole of Ilex Forest's night grass table.
Same grass, opposite shifts (HeartGold; Weedle in SoulSilver).

ecotypes.name: Rooted settler
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that leans further into the plant side of its life: it roots in harder and longer (Ingrain) and draws energy from light (Synthesis) instead of wandering. Fits stable, fertile clearings where staying put pays better than seeding new ground.
ecotypes.behavior: Wanders less and stays planted for days, leaves held up to the light.

ecotypes.name: Blade-leaf
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that arms its leaves: sharp-edged leaves thrown or slashed at attackers. Fits grassland and forest edges with more grazers or predators, where the leaves a buried Oddish leaves showing (43.8) are what gets bitten.
ecotypes.behavior: Fights back with its leaves instead of shrieking and staying put.

ecotypes.name: Distraction dancer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that defuses attackers with behaviour rather than chemistry: a confusing dance, a disarming display, tickling. Fits places with many casual predators, and it foreshadows the line's later dancing (Bellossom).
ecotypes.behavior: Dances and fusses when cornered.

open_questions: What do its seeds grow into, and how do seeds relate to eggs?
Does it photosynthesise with its exposed leaves by day, or only absorb moonlight?
Does it ever take energy from other organisms (Absorb, Mega Drain), or only from soil and light?
Who are the enemies it hides from by day (43.8)?
Does its planting enrich or deplete the soil?
When does the line start eating animals: at Gloom, or earlier?

contradictions.text: How much of it is above ground by day? Crystal says it stays in the cold underground to avoid the sun (43.5) and Red/Blue that it keeps its face buried (43.1); Emerald says it leaves its leaves exposed (43.8).
contradictions.note: Compatible if only the leaves show, but a plant with leaves in the open isn't fully avoiding the sun.

folklore.text: It is said to walk nearly 1,000 feet (about 300 m) a night on its two roots.
folklore.note: Hearsay in the entry itself ('it is said'). The same entry gives its scientific name, cited under People.

Paras.summary: A small bug that carries its own parasite. Paras burrows to suck and gnaw tree roots and draws juice from trunks, and the mushrooms on its back, called tochukaso, grow by taking nutrients from it; one entry says they take most of its food, another that they order the bug to feed. The spores reach it at birth, the mushrooms grow as it grows, and in Parasect the mushroom has taken over. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is met in Ilex Forest's grass at every hour, least often by day.

anatomy.text: A small bug (0.3 m, 5.4 kg) with mushrooms growing on its back.
The mushrooms are called tochukaso and are described as parasitic: they grow large by drawing nutrients from the bug host.
anatomy.analogy: Tochukaso is the Japanese reading of 冬虫夏草 ('winter worm, summer grass'), the name for Ophiocordyceps sinensis and related insect-parasitic fungi; O. sinensis infects ghost-moth caterpillars in the soil of the Tibetan Plateau and fruits from the dead larva.

anatomy.text: The mushrooms grow with the host, sprouting and enlarging as the bug's body grows.
Its two types read as its two partners: Bug for the host, Grass for the mushroom (the games have no fungus type).

diet.text: It burrows to suck tree roots, or burrows under the ground to gnaw on them.
diet.analogy: Cicada nymphs spend years underground feeding on the sap of tree roots.

diet.text: The mushroom orders it to extract juice from tree trunks.
The mushrooms absorb most of the nutrition: the bug does the feeding and the fungus takes most of the food.

habitat.text: Forest, and underground among tree roots.
Its evolved form stays in dark, damp places, a preference not of the bug but of the mushroom.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's grass (a 5% slot at every hour, plus 10% more in the morning and at night), National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, Mt. Moon's caves and the Johto Safari Zone.
Its ability Dry Skin (it loses HP in heat; water restores it) fits a damp-loving animal.

behavior.text: It burrows.

It is present in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning, by day and at night, least often by day (5% against 15%). That rests on the time-of-day split in the tables and fits the line's liking for dark, damp places; a table rate isn't abundance.
The fungus directs at least some of what it does: it orders the bug to extract juice from tree trunks.
behavior.analogy: Fungal control of host behaviour is real: Ophiocordyceps unilateralis makes infected carpenter ants climb vegetation and clamp their jaws onto a leaf before the fungus fruits from the ant's body.

social.text: Nothing is said for Paras. As Parasect they infest large trees in numbers and move to another tree all at once, so the adults at least gather.

reproduction.text: It is doused with mushroom spores when it is born.
When nothing is left to extract from the bug, the mushrooms on Parasect's back leave spores on the bug's egg: the fungus passes from parent to offspring at the egg.
reproduction.analogy: Passing a symbiont or parasite from parent to offspring is vertical transmission; it is common in insects, as with the Buchnera bacteria that aphids pass to their young.

reproduction.text: Bug and Grass egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio.

defense.text: No Paras entry describes a defence; what follows comes from its ability and moves.
Effect Spore: contact with it may paralyse, poison or put an attacker to sleep. Read biologically, the mushroom's spores defend the pair.
Stun Spore and Poison Powder (Lv 6) and Spore (Lv 17) make spores its main weapons; Slash (22) and X-Scissor (43) are its claws.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: Paras becomes Parasect at level 24. In Parasect the mushroom has grown larger than the host's body and controls it.
In Parasect the bug host is drained of energy and the mushrooms appear to do all the thinking.

Read in order, the entries trace an infection: spores at birth (46.3), mushrooms growing with the young bug (46.9, 46.10) and taking most of its food (46.2), a mushroom in control of the adult (47.1, 47.9), and spores passed to the next egg once the bug is spent (47.5).
Parasitism or symbiosis? The entries call the mushroom parasitic (46.6 to 46.8) and the adult a host-parasite pair (47.1), and none describes any benefit to the bug. Recorded here as parasitism.
The spores may protect the bug, which would make the young relationship partly mutualistic: Effect Spore and the spore moves are its only described defences.
life_cycle.note: Rests on game mechanics only; no entry says the bug benefits.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Feeding: Scratch (Lv 1), Leech Life (11) and Giga Drain (33). Two draining moves suit a root- and sap-sucker.
Growth (27) and Aromatherapy (38) read as the mushroom's moves, growing and scent. Aromatherapy cures the whole party's status problems, an odd move for a parasite that drains its host.
moves_in_the_wild.note: Assigning moves to host or fungus is a reading, not something the games do.

ecology.text: A root and sap feeder (trophic level 2) carrying a fungus that feeds on it (the fungus is a parasite at level 3).
Hard on trees in numbers: as Parasect they infest large trees en masse, drain the lower trunk and roots, and when the tree dies move on to another all at once. Paras is the first stage of that.
By killing trees, the line would create deadwood and gaps in the canopy, but no member of the community is described eating deadwood.
ecology.note: A gap in the reconstructed web: no decomposer is described.

ecology.text: The tochukaso is the community's only described fungus, and it is a parasite of a living host, not a decomposer.

Spoink, which is in Ilex Forest only through the Hoenn Sound on the radio, loves eating mushrooms that grow underground, which makes it the community's one described fungus-eater. Whether it eats tochukaso is unknown.
ecology.note: No entry links the two.

humans.text: Tochukaso are highly valued as a medicine for extending life (see Folklore for the claim itself).
humans.analogy: Ophiocordyceps sinensis is among the most expensive traditional medicines in China and the Himalaya, sold as a tonic.

humans.text: Parasect's spores are used as herbal medicine in China.
If tochukaso are valued, people would collect Paras; no entry describes this.

homestead.text: A medicinal crop, if the medicine claims hold: tochukaso grow on Paras's back and are valued for long life. Harvesting would need to leave the host alive and the mushroom able to regrow; nobody has described whether it does.
homestead.note: Its medicinal value is claimed, not shown.

homestead.text: Keep it out of the orchard and the Glasshouse: it feeds on tree roots, and its evolved form kills trees in groups.
It needs dark, damp, cool places and water (Dry Skin), so a cellar or cave would suit it better than a sunny yard; it already lives in Mt. Moon's caves as well as forest.

niche.foraging: burrows to suck and gnaw tree roots and extracts juice from trunks; the fungus on its back takes most of the nutrition
niche.note: Activity is read from presence in all three time-of-day tables.

relationships.note: Parasitism: the mushroom draws nutrients from the bug, takes most of its food, and as Parasect controls it.
Described for Parasect, which drains trees until they die; Paras's root-feeding is the start of it.
Spoink loves mushrooms that grow underground; if it eats tochukaso, it eats part of the pair. Spoink is radio-only (Hoenn Sound).
Both draw on what's below ground: roots for Paras, soil nutrients for Oddish.
Ilex Forest's night grass and Mt. Moon's caves.

ecotypes.name: Lure-and-bite
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that adds animal food to root sap: a scent lure to bring small animals close, a bite, and a strike at whatever turns to flee. Fits poor soils where roots yield little.
ecotypes.behavior: Sits scented at a burrow mouth and snaps at visitors.

ecotypes.name: Stone-claw digger
ecotypes.reading: A lineage built for hard ground: hardened claws for burrowing through stony or root-bound soil, and Counter for whatever digs it up. Fits rocky ground and caves such as Mt. Moon, where Paras also lives.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs deeper and hits back when unearthed.

ecotypes.name: Bug-led
ecotypes.reading: A lineage in which the bug keeps the upper hand for longer: fast, with venomous claws, able to forage beyond the dark, damp places the mushroom prefers (47.3). Fits drier, more open woodland.
ecotypes.behavior: Moves about more by day and burrows less.

ecotypes.name: Mind-mushroom
ecotypes.reading: The tochukaso already gives the host orders (46.5) and seems to do the thinking in Parasect (47.2); a psychic attack in the lineage reads as that control turned outward, against attackers. Fits crowded infestations where many Paras share one tree.
ecotypes.behavior: Unsettles attackers instead of fleeing them.

open_questions: Does the bug get anything from the mushroom, such as protection by its spores, or is it pure parasitism?
Is every Paras infected at birth (46.3), or can an uninfected Paras exist?
Does the fungus eventually kill the host (47.5 'nothing's left to extract from the bug')?
Which trees does it feed on, and how much harm does a single Paras do?
Do the medicinal claims hold, and could tochukaso be harvested without harming the host?
Does Spoink eat tochukaso?

contradictions.text: Sucks or gnaws? Red/Blue says it burrows to suck tree roots (46.1); Yellow says it gnaws on them (46.2).
contradictions.note: It may do both; recorded because the feeding mode matters for whether it takes sap or tissue.

folklore.text: Tochukaso are 'highly valued as a medicine for extending life' and 'valued as a medicine for long life'.
folklore.note: A belief the entries record about the mushroom's value; they don't say the medicine works.

Pikachu.summary: A small forest mouse that stores electricity in pouches on its cheeks and uses it for almost everything. It lives in groups, monitors its surroundings with its tail raised, and when several gather their combined charge can build into a lightning storm. The Gold and HeartGold Pokédex call it intelligent enough to roast hard Berries with electricity until they are tender, and Ruby notes the blackened Berries left when it overdoes it. One Platinum entry has it recharging a weakened companion with a shock, and the young, Pichu, play at touching tails to set off sparks.

anatomy.text: A small quadruped (0.4 m, 6.0 kg) with electricity-storing pouches or sacs on both cheeks.
The stored charge can be released in a single burst equal to a lightning bolt.
anatomy.analogy: The strongest real electric animal, the electric eel (Electrophorus), produces up to several hundred volts from stacks of modified muscle cells; a lightning bolt is many orders of magnitude beyond that.

anatomy.text: The tail is held up as a monitoring organ, and is sometimes struck by lightning in that pose.

diet.text: It eats Berries, and roasts hard ones with electricity to make them tender enough to eat.
diet.analogy: No wild animal cooks. The nearest real behaviour is food processing, such as bearded capuchins (Sapajus libidinosus) cracking hard nuts open with stone hammers.

diet.text: It sometimes misjudges: a blackened Berry is evidence of a Pikachu that overdid its charge.
Whether it also feeds on electricity, as Magnemite does, is not said; its charge is described as generated or gathered, not eaten.

habitat.text: A forest animal that lives with others of its kind; its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver its only wild home is Kanto's Viridian Forest, uncommon at any hour (5%) with an extra rare daytime slot (1%); Johto has none. Gold and Silver put it on Kanto's Route 2.
In Red, Blue, FireRed and LeafGreen it is common in Kanto's Power Plant (25%), alongside Magnemite, Magneton, Voltorb and Electabuzz: an electrical habitat as well as a forest one.
Pichu is found wild only in Sinnoh's Trophy Garden, where Diamond and Pearl add a morning slot; in Crystal it comes as an egg on Route 34.

behavior.text: Vigilant: it keeps its tail raised to check its surroundings.
It tests new things with electricity: whenever it comes across something new it blasts it with a jolt.
Its cheek pouches seem to charge at night while it sleeps, and it may discharge when drowsy after waking, so it sleeps at night.
Sleeping at night implies a day-active animal.
Intelligent, by the Gold and HeartGold entries.

social.text: It lives in groups in the forest, and several together can build up enough electricity to cause lightning storms.
It helps its own kind: it occasionally recharges a weakened fellow Pikachu with an electric shock.
Crackling from the cheek pouches signals wariness, a warning others can hear.
social.analogy: A warning display before attack, comparable in function to a rattlesnake's rattle.

social.text: Pichu play together by touching tails to set off sparks, which seems to be a test of courage; shorting out with another Pichu makes it cry.

reproduction.text: Field and Fairy egg groups, an even sex ratio, 10 egg cycles (short), medium growth. Pichu is a baby Pokémon in the Undiscovered group and can't breed.
Short incubation and a small, common animal suggest a fast-breeding species, but nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding.

defense.text: Electric defence: threatened, it looses charges from its cheek sacs; angered, it discharges its stored energy at once.
It bites if its tail is yanked.
Static, its ability, may paralyse anything that touches it.
Its own level-up list adds Double Team (Lv 18) and Agility (Lv 34), evasion and speed: a small animal that dodges first.

senses.text: The raised tail monitors its surroundings; what it detects is not said.
Raichu's ears stand straight up when its pouches are fully charged, so the line's ears respond to charge state.

life_cycle.text: Pichu (0.3 m, 2.0 kg) becomes Pikachu when it levels up with high friendship; Pikachu becomes Raichu (0.8 m, 30.0 kg, upright) on exposure to a Thunder Stone.
Storage is learned with age: Pichu's cheek pouches are small, it can't hold much electricity, discharges when startled or amused, and shocks itself; it gets better at holding power as it grows older.
Raichu manages a larger charge: it grows aggressive as charge builds and calms itself by discharging through its tail into the ground, leaving scorched patches near its nest.
Read as development, the line goes from leaking charge, to storing and using it deliberately, to having to vent it to stay calm.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its level-up repertoire is electrical and evasive: Thunder Shock (Lv 1), Thunder Wave (Lv 10), Quick Attack, Double Team, Thunderbolt (Lv 26), Agility, Discharge (Lv 37), Light Screen and Thunder (Lv 45).
Discharge, which hits everything around it, is the closest move to the uncontrolled release of a startled or angry animal.
Tail Whip (Lv 5) and Slam (Lv 21) both use the tail it otherwise holds up as a monitor.

ecology.text: A forest frugivore (trophic level about 2), and possibly a minor disperser of Berry seeds, though roasting would probably kill them.
Groups can trigger lightning storms, and a raised tail draws lightning: a fire and disturbance risk to the forest it lives in.
Raichu leaves scorched patches near its nest, small disturbances in the ground cover.

humans.text: Pichu can zap even adult humans, and surprises itself when it does.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver a Pikachu is offered in trade in Saffron City; in Crystal a Pikachu is a Game Corner prize in Celadon City; in Yellow it is the starter.

homestead.text: Cooking help in the kitchen: it softens hard Berries with electricity. Expect some to come out blackened.
Small-scale electricity: it stores charge in its cheeks and can recharge another Pikachu; whether it can be persuaded to charge a battery is untested.
homestead.note: Recharging a companion is canon; charging equipment is the capability record's guess.

homestead.text: Lightning risk on the highland: a group can build a lightning storm, and a raised tail can be struck. Don't house many together near the Glasshouse or timber buildings.
Introduce new tools and equipment carefully: it jolts anything new it comes across.
Pichu in the nursery will shock carers, and itself, when startled; Blackthorn's dry winter air makes that worse, since Pichu charge more easily when the air is very dry.
A small, alert lookout: its raised tail monitors its surroundings and its crackling warns of trouble.
Needs: company of its own kind, Berries, and somewhere to sleep undisturbed at night while its pouches recharge.

niche.foraging: gathers Berries and softens hard ones with electricity before eating
niche.note: Activity is read from its sleeping at night (25.7); encounter tables give it at all hours.

relationships.note: Its tail is struck by lightning (25.4); Raichu gathers electricity from the air (26.5); Pichu charge more easily under thunderclouds (172.4).
Kanto Power Plant in Red, Blue, FireRed and LeafGreen; an electrical community.
By Thunder Stone, an object people supply.

ecotypes.name: Storm capacitor
ecotypes.reading: A store-and-release lineage: Charge builds up power for the next electric move, Bide absorbs punishment and returns it doubled, and Reversal hits hardest when it is nearly beaten. It is the cheek-pouch canon (pent-up energy released in one burst) made into a fighting style. Fits exposed ridges and hilltops with frequent thunderstorms, where charge comes easily.
ecotypes.behavior: Holds back, soaks up, then releases everything at once.

ecotypes.name: Kin keeper
ecotypes.reading: A caring lineage built on the Platinum canon of recharging a weakened companion: Wish heals whoever is in its place next turn, Present can heal or harm, and Encore holds an attacker to one move while others act. Fits dense forest groups where weak members are kept going rather than left.
ecotypes.behavior: Stays close to injured groupmates; tends rather than flees.

ecotypes.name: Spark-sparrer
ecotypes.reading: Play-fighting kept into adulthood: Fake Out startles, Double Slap is a contact contest of quick light blows, and Tickle weakens without injuring. Low-harm moves that settle disputes, like Pichu's tail-touching tests of courage. Fits large, crowded groups where real fights would be costly.
ecotypes.behavior: Settles rank with sparring rather than shocks.

open_questions: Where does its electricity come from? Generated in sleep (25.7), gathered from storms (172.4) or from the air (26.5), or all three?
Does it eat anything besides Berries?
How does recharging a weakened Pikachu (25.13) work, and is it common or rare?
What does the raised tail actually sense?
Is there a wild population anywhere in Johto? The HeartGold tables have none.
Is it ever killed by the lightning its tail attracts (25.4)?

contradictions.text: Group lightning storms: Red and Blue say several Pikachu together 'could' cause lightning storms; LeafGreen, with the same sentence, says they 'can'.
contradictions.note: Minor: possibility versus fact.

contradictions.text: What Raichu's grounded tail does: Ruby, Diamond and Platinum say it discharges excess electricity into the ground; Sapphire says Raichu plants its tail in the ground to search for electricity.
contradictions.note: Venting versus gathering through the same posture.

Pineco.summary: A sit-and-wait predator of the forest canopy that builds its own armour. Pineco hangs from a branch inside a case of tree bark it glues on with a fluid that sets in air, waits for flying insects to come close, and barely moves otherwise. It passes for a pinecone, which keeps birds from treating it as food; if its tree is shaken while it feeds it drops and explodes. In Johto it lives in the trees themselves: every wild Pineco in the Johto games is found by shaking a tree.

anatomy.text: A small, rounded body (0.6 m, 7.2 kg) wrapped in a case it builds and thickens itself from layers of tree bark.
It secretes a fluid that it spits out to glue bark to its body; the fluid hardens on contact with air.
anatomy.analogy: Bagworm moth caterpillars (Psychidae), whose name this Pokémon's category borrows, bind plant fragments into a portable case with silk that likewise sets once it is spun.

anatomy.text: The case is heavy relative to the animal, and the weight doesn't hinder it; the armour costs it mobility rather than effort, which fits an animal that hardly moves.

diet.text: It eats flying insects, which it waits for rather than chases.
It feeds from a hanging position on a branch and is exposed to disturbance while eating.
Its prey are most likely small, non-Pokémon insects: the flying Bug Pokémon it shares trees with in Ilex Forest (Butterfree 1.1 m, Beedrill 1.0 m) are larger than Pineco itself.
Bug Bite, which it learns early (Lv 9), is a biting attack and the most plausible reading of how it takes prey.

habitat.text: A forest animal that lives in trees, hanging from branches.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is found only by Headbutting trees, and the tree tables put it almost everywhere in Johto with trees, from New Bark Town to Ecruteak City; in Ilex Forest it is on the rarer tree table.

In Sinnoh (Diamond, Pearl, Platinum) it appears in Eterna Forest and on Routes 203, 204, 210 and 229 only when Pokémon Emerald is in the second slot, so it is not a native Sinnoh animal in the games' own terms.
Its microhabitat is the canopy and branches rather than the trunk or ground; it reaches the ground only when it falls.

behavior.text: Sedentary: it doesn't move about much on its own.
An ambush (sit-and-wait) forager: it hangs patiently and lets prey come to it.
behavior.analogy: The same strategy as orb-weavers and ambush bugs: low energy spent, low encounter rate, long waits.

behavior.text: Activity pattern isn't stated anywhere; HeartGold's tree tables don't split it by time of day.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or interaction with its own kind; the sedentary ambush life suggests it lives alone on its branch.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio; nothing in the Pokédex describes how it breeds or where it lays.

defense.text: Masquerade: it looks just like a pinecone, and its shell protects it from bird Pokémon that peck it by mistake.
defense.analogy: Masquerade (resembling an inedible object) rather than camouflage (blending into the background), as in caterpillars that pass for twigs or bird droppings.

defense.text: Last-resort defence: if its tree is shaken while it eats, it drops to the ground and explodes without warning.
defense.analogy: Comparable to autothysis in exploding ants (Colobopsis), where a worker ruptures its own body to defend the colony; Pineco's explosion is not described as fatal to it.

defense.text: Its moves line up with the canon: Protect at Lv 1 and Iron Defense later (withdrawing into armour), Self-Destruct from Lv 6 and Explosion at Lv 34 (the drop-and-explode defence), and Sturdy (it can't be knocked out in one blow).

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. An ambush predator of flying insects must detect prey approaching through the air, so vision or vibration sense is implied but not described; as Forretress its eyes are the only part visible through the shell.
